nodes.title: Standard Neron n-gons over an arbitrary base, the 1-gon, and the translation action (2.1.2)
nodes.statement: For n >= 1 and any scheme S the standard n-gon C_n over S is the coequalizer of the two closed immersions of the disjoint union of Z/nZ copies of S into the disjoint union of Z/nZ copies of P^1_S (0-section of copy i glued to the infinity-section of copy i+1); this colimit exists and its formation commutes with arbitrary base change (for n >= 2 it is the base change of the gluing of the Spec Z[X_i,Y_i]/(X_i Y_i)). The Z/nZ-action on C_n is free; for d | n with d > 1 there is a unique map C_n -> C_d compatible with P^1_S x Z/nZ -> P^1_S x Z/dZ, and it is a finite etale dZ/nZ-torsor. The quotient C_n -> C_{1,n} by Z/nZ exists as a finite etale Z/nZ-torsor compatible with base change and is independent of n: this is the standard 1-gon C_1, proper with canonical section 1 and a finite map P^1_S -> C_1 gluing the sections 0 and infinity. The action of G_m x Z/nZ on P^1_S x Z/nZ descends uniquely to + : C_n^sm x_S C_n -> C_n, an action extending the group law of C_n^sm = G_m x Z/nZ, compatible with base change and with change of n.
hypotheses: n >= 1 an integer; S an arbitrary scheme (no noetherian or characteristic hypothesis)
for the 1-gon: the Z/nZ-action on C_n (n > 1) is free and each orbit lies in an open affine, which is what SGA 3 Exp. V Thm 4.1 requires
proofSteps: Construct C_n for n >= 2 by gluing Spec Z[X_i,Y_i]/(X_iY_i) along Y_i = 1/X_{i+1}-type identifications and base change to S (Cesnavicius Remark 2.1.2); the gluing commutes with base change.
The projection P^1_S x Z/nZ -> P^1_S x Z/dZ induces C_n -> C_d, invariant under dZ/nZ acting freely, realizing C_n as a finite etale dZ/nZ-torsor over C_d (Conrad (2.1.1)).

Apply SGA 3 Exp. V Thm 4.1 (quotient by a free finite group action with orbits in affines) to get C_n -> C_{1,n}; the torsor maps (2.1.1) identify the C_{1,n} for varying n, defining C_1 (Conrad p. 5).
Descend the G_m x Z/nZ-action on the normalization P^1_S x Z/nZ to C_n, obtaining (2.1.2) (Conrad p. 5; DR II 1.9 for the same construction over Spec Z).
acceptance: C_n^sm = G_m x Z/nZ and C_n^sing is a disjoint union of n copies of S (proof of Cesnavicius Lemma 2.1.10).
For d | n the map C_n -> C_d is a dZ/nZ-torsor and restricts to the quotient map on smooth loci.

Negative check: the plane cubic y^2 z = x^3 - x^2 z named on Conrad p. 5 is NOT a model of C_1 over Z (its node has tangent slopes +-i and it is cuspidal in characteristic 2; the map t -> (t^2+1, t(t^2+1)) identifies t = i and t = -i, not 0 and infinity); a split nodal cubic such as y^2 z + xyz = x^3 must be used instead (worker's computation, see gap).

nodes.title: DR semistable (stable) genus-one curves: definition, openness, fibre classification, p_* O = O and the dualizing sheaf
nodes.statement: A curve over S is a separated flat finitely presented morphism whose fibres are non-empty of pure dimension 1. A stable genus-one curve in the sense of Deligne-Rapoport (Conrad: DR semistable genus-1 curve) over a scheme, algebraic space or algebraic stack S is a (proper) curve over S each of whose geometric fibres is either a proper smooth connected genus-one curve or a Neron polygon (DR II Def. 1.4); equivalently geometric fibres are connected and semistable with trivial dualizing sheaf (Conrad Def. 2.1.2), the equivalence over an algebraically closed field being DR II 1.2-1.3. For p : C -> S proper flat of finite presentation the set of s with C_s a stable genus-one curve is open (DR II 1.5; Conrad Lemma 2.1.3). For a stable genus-one curve p : C -> S one has p_* O_C = O_S universally, omega_{C/S} and p_*(omega_{C/S}) are invertible, and the canonical map p^* p_*(omega_{C/S}) -> omega_{C/S} is an isomorphism (DR II 1.6). The non-smooth locus C^sing is the closed subscheme defined by the first Fitting ideal of Omega^1_{C/S}, of formation compatible with base change (Conrad p. 5-6; Cesnavicius Def. 2.1.7, Remark 2.1.8).
hypotheses: For openness (DR II 1.5): p : C -> S proper, flat and of finite presentation
For DR II 1.6: C -> S a stable genus-one curve; the proof reduces to S noetherian and uses EGA III 7.8.8 and coherent duality (DR I 2)
proofSteps: Over an algebraically closed field, a reduced connected genus-one curve with only ordinary double points and trivial dualizing sheaf is smooth or a Neron polygon: count components, genera and double points of the normalization (DR II Lemma 1.3, using 1.2).
Openness: reducedness, connectedness, pure dimension one, genus one and ordinary quadratic singularities are open conditions; openness of omega = O follows from the proof of 1.6 (DR II 1.5).

p_* O_C = O_S universally by EGA III 7.8.8 since geometric fibres are connected and reduced; fibres are local complete intersections so omega_{C/S} is invertible; R^1 p_* O is locally free with base change and duality gives the same for p_* omega; reduce 1.6.1 to an algebraically closed field (DR II 1.6).
acceptance: For the standard n-gon, H^0(C, omega_C) is one-dimensional and generated by the form equal to dx/x on each copy of P^1 (DR II 1.2 proof).
Pic^0 of a Neron polygon over an algebraically closed field is G_m (DR II Lemma 1.7(i)).

nodes.title: Generalized elliptic curves, their morphisms, and agreement with elliptic curves on the smooth locus
nodes.statement: A generalized elliptic curve over S is a stable genus-one curve p : C -> S with an S-morphism + : C^reg x_S C -> C such that (a) + restricts to a commutative group scheme structure on the smooth locus C^reg, (b) + is an action of C^reg on C, and (c) for every geometric point s of S with C_s singular the translations by points of C^reg_s act by rotations on the graph Gamma(C_s) of irreducible components (DR II Def. 1.12); the identity section e lies in C^sm(S) (Conrad Def. 2.1.4). Under (a)-(b), (c) holds exactly on an open and closed subset of S over which C^reg acts trivially on Pic^0_{C/S} (DR II Prop. 1.13), so (c) may be replaced by triviality of the induced action on Pic^0 (Cesnavicius Def. 2.1.3 and Remark 2.1.4, via DR II 1.7(ii), 1.13). A morphism E -> E' is an S-map carrying E^sm into E'^sm and inducing a homomorphism of smooth loci; by universal schematic density of E^sm (EGA IV_3 11.10.4, 11.10.10) it is automatically equivariant for the actions. A smooth generalized elliptic curve is exactly an elliptic curve; every elliptic curve is a generalized elliptic curve, and a generalized elliptic curve is an elliptic curve over the open subscheme of S where it is smooth (DR p. 178; Cesnavicius Remark 2.1.4). Over an algebraically closed field a generalized elliptic curve is an elliptic curve or isomorphic to a standard n-gon with the structure (2.1.2) (DR II 1.15; Conrad p. 5).
hypotheses: S an arbitrary scheme (DR also allow algebraic spaces and stacks as bases for Def. 1.4)
For the Pic^0 reformulation: Pic^0_{C/S} as a semi-abelian algebraic space (Conrad 2.2 via Artin and BLR 9.2/8) or scheme (DR II 2.6(i) with BLR 6.6/2, Cesnavicius footnote 1)
proofSteps: DR II Lemma 1.7(ii): an automorphism of a Neron polygon is trivial on Pic^0 iff it acts by rotations on Gamma(C).

DR II Lemma 1.14 (Conrad Lemma 2.2.1 for algebraic spaces): for two endomorphisms g, h of a semi-abelian S-group there is an open and closed V in S universal for g_T = h_T; applied to translations on Pic^0 x C^reg it shows the locus U of Prop. 1.13 is closed, and openness is proved together with 1.15.
Equivariance of morphisms: E^sm is S-universally schematically dense in E and E' is separated (Conrad p. 5; Cesnavicius Remark 2.1.13).
Smooth locus: if C is smooth, (c) is vacuous and (a)-(b) are the axioms of an elliptic curve; conversely the Pic^0 condition holds on (E^sm)^0 by DR II 1.14 (Cesnavicius Remark 2.1.4).
acceptance: The standard n-gon with (2.1.2) satisfies (a)-(c); translations by the component of index i rotate Gamma(C) by i (DR II 1.11).
The zero map and finite etale S-maps are morphisms in this sense (Conrad p. 5).
Restricting a generalized elliptic curve to S minus the degeneracy locus gives the elliptic-curve object of the existing affine theory; no further structure is added there.

nodes.title: Automorphisms of the standard n-gon: mu_n x Z/2Z, finite flat of rank 2n and etale iff n is invertible
nodes.statement: For the standard n-gon C over Spec Z with its generalized elliptic curve structure, Aut(C,+) is identified with the semidirect product of {e, tau} (tau the involution extending inversion) and mu_n, where a section zeta of mu_n acts on the i-th component by x -> zeta^i x; the subgroup acting trivially on Pic^0 is mu_n (DR II Prop. 1.10). The inversion commutes with mu_n, so Aut(C) = mu_n x Z/2Z (Cesnavicius Lemma 2.1.6). Consequently, if E -> S has n-gon geometric fibres and S equals its degeneracy locus, Isom(E, C_n) -> S is finite locally free of rank 2n, etale if n is a unit on S, and E becomes isomorphic to C_n over it (Conrad Cor. 3.1.3); in residue characteristic p | n the automorphism group scheme contains the non-etale mu_p.
hypotheses: n >= 1; the scheme-level statements hold over any base S
Conrad Cor. 3.1.3 assumes all geometric fibres are n-gons and S = S^{infinity,f}
proofSteps: DR II Lemma 1.8: exact sequence 0 -> G_m^n -> Aut(C) -> Aut(Gamma(C)) -> 0 for automorphisms of the underlying scheme.
Compatibility with + forces lambda_i lambda_j = lambda_{i+j}, i.e. a homomorphism Z/n -> G_m, hence a section of mu_n (DR II 1.10 proof).
Cesnavicius: every generalized elliptic curve automorphism of a base change of E commutes with inversion on E^sm, so Z/2Z is central (universal schematic density of E^sm).
Conrad Cor. 3.1.3: fppf-locally over S the Isom-scheme is the Aut-scheme of C_n (Lemma 2.1.10), which is finite locally free of rank 2n.
acceptance: For n = 1, Aut(C_1) = Z/2Z, so a degenerate 1-gon fibre becomes the standard 1-gon over a degree-2 finite etale cover (Conrad Cor. 3.1.3).
Over F_p with p | n, mu_p is an infinitesimal subgroup of Aut(C_n) (source of the non-Deligne-Mumford points of R13.2).

nodes.title: Degeneracy locus: fppf-local n-gon structure and compatibility of S^infinity with arbitrary base change
nodes.statement: Let p : C -> S be a generalized elliptic curve. There is a locally finite family (S_n)_{n>=1} of disjoint closed subschemes of S whose union is the image of the non-smoothness subscheme C^sing, such that over S_n the curve C is fppf-locally isomorphic to the standard n-gon (DR II Prop. 1.15; Conrad Lemma 2.1.10). Defining S^{infinity,f} as the scheme-theoretic image of C^sing, its formation commutes with arbitrary base change on S (Conrad Thm. 2.1.12), although for arbitrary stable genus-one curves only the inclusion T^{infinity} c S^{infinity} x_S T holds (Conrad (2.1.3), Example 2.1.11). The map C^sing -> S^{infinity} is finite etale of degree n over S^{infinity,n} (Cesnavicius Lemma 2.1.10).
hypotheses: C -> S a generalized elliptic curve over an arbitrary scheme S (base change compatibility fails for general stable genus-one curves)
proofSteps: DR II Lemma 1.16: if an automorphism g permutes the singular points of an n-gon fibre transitively, then near s the curve is etale-locally the standard n-gon over the image of C^sing; the proof uses the etale-local form xy = t of an ordinary double point (DR I 5.3), blows up C^sing and uses Stein factorization.

Apply 1.16 to a translation x+ by a section meeting the component of index one, which exists etale-locally; extract an n-th root of the resulting G_m-parameter fppf-locally (etale-locally if n is invertible) to reach the standard structure (1.9) (DR II end of proof of 1.15, p. 182).
Conrad Thm. 2.1.12: fppf-locally over S^{infinity} the curve is a standard polygon, for which S^infinity = S (Example 2.1.9), so (2.1.3) is an equality after an fppf cover and hence before.
acceptance: Conrad Example 2.1.11: for the twisted 2-gon C_{a,a'} over A = k[eps,eps']/(eps,eps')^2 with a = eps, a' = eps', the non-smoothness locus is all of Spec A but becomes Spec k after base change to eps = eps'; this must not occur for generalized elliptic curves.
For Tate_n over Z[[q^{1/n}]] the degeneracy locus is cut out by q^{1/n} (Conrad Section 2.5).

nodes.title: A pointed nodal genus-one family need not carry a generalized elliptic curve structure (Conrad Example 2.1.11 and Remark 2.1.13)
nodes.statement: Over a local artin ring A with elements a, a' in the maximal ideal, gluing Spec A[t,t']/(tt'-a) and Spec A[u,u']/(uu'-a') along the complements of the origins gives an A-flat twisted 2-gon C_{a,a'}, a stable genus-one curve whose closed fibre is the standard 2-gon, and whose non-smoothness locus in the base is cut out by (a) intersect (a'). For A = k[eps,eps']/(eps,eps')^2, a = eps, a' = eps', the formation of this locus does not commute with base change, so by Conrad Thm. 2.1.12 no generalized elliptic curve structure exists on C_{a,a'}, even fpqc-locally on the base. By contrast a stable genus-one curve with geometrically irreducible fibres and a section in the smooth locus has a unique generalized elliptic curve structure with that identity (DR II 2.7, as cited by Conrad Remark 2.1.13).
hypotheses: k a field; A = k[eps,eps']/(eps,eps')^2 for the explicit failure
The positive statement (DR II 2.7) needs geometrically irreducible fibres and e in C^sm(S)
proofSteps: Fitting-ideal computation on the two charts shows the non-smoothness locus of C_{a,a'} is V((a) intersect (a')) (Conrad Example 2.1.11).
(eps) intersect (eps') = 0 in A, but after eps = eps' the locus is Spec k, so base change compatibility fails.
Theorem 2.1.12 (previous node) forbids this for generalized elliptic curves, fpqc-locally as well.
acceptance: Any formal statement 'every pointed stable genus-one curve with n-gon degenerate fibres is a generalized elliptic curve' must be rejected by this example.

nodes.title: Deligne-Rapoport construction principle: an action trivial on Pic^0 and transitive on components gives a unique generalized elliptic curve structure
nodes.statement: Let p : C -> S be a stable genus-one curve with a section e in C^sm(S), and let G be a commutative flat S-group scheme locally of finite presentation acting on C such that (3.1.1) G acts trivially on Pic^0_{C/S} and (3.1.2) for every geometric point s, G(s) acts transitively on the irreducible components of C_s. Then C has a unique generalized elliptic curve structure with identity e such that each g in G(T) acts on C_T by translation by g(e) in C^sm(T), and every automorphism of C commuting with G (and satisfying 3.1.1) is a translation (DR II Thm. 3.2; Conrad Thm. 2.2.2). Special case (Conrad Cor. 2.2.3): if D in C^sm is an S-ample relative effective Cartier divisor with a commutative S-group structure and an action on C extending its group law, this extends to a generalized elliptic curve structure iff D acts trivially on Pic^0_{C/S}; the structure is then unique, triviality may be checked on geometric fibres, and the locus of fibres where it holds is open and closed in S.
hypotheses: C -> S a stable genus-one curve with e in C^sm(S)
G commutative, flat, locally of finite presentation over S, acting on C; (3.1.1) and (3.1.2) hold
In Cor. 2.2.3: D S-ample relative effective Cartier divisor supported in C^sm; for the fibrewise criterion G = D finite locally free
proofSteps: (A) fppf-locally near a geometric point with an n-gon fibre, choose g in G whose image generates the cyclic rotation group of Gamma(C_s); DR II 1.16 gives (3.1.4) and 1.13 gives (3.1.3) nearby (DR II p. 194).

(B) case G = Z: by 1.16 reduce to fibres all smooth or n-gons; g^n e lies fibrewise in the identity component, so by Lemma 3.3 g^n = lambda + x for a section lambda of Pic^0; replacing g by g_1 with g_1^n = Id gives a free Z/n-action with integral geometric fibres of C/(Z/n); DR II 2.7 gives the structure on the quotient and 1.17 lifts it to C (pp. 194-195).

Conrad Cor. 2.2.3: ampleness of D makes D(s) transitive on components; for triviality on Pic^0 apply Lemma 2.2.1 to the universal action on A x G to get an open and closed V in G, whose complement has open and closed image; its complement U represents triviality.
Conrad works with Pic^0_{C/S} as a semi-abelian algebraic space (Artin [Ar, Thm 7.3], SGA 6 XIII 4.7, BLR 9.2/14 and 9.2/8); DR use the Picard scheme.
acceptance: For D = Z/nZ in the standard n-gon with rotation action, Cor. 2.2.3 recovers (2.1.2).
Formal Tate curves: the rotation action (2.5.1) of Z/nZ on each infinitesimal neighbourhood gives a unique generalized elliptic curve structure (Conrad p. 17).

nodes.title: Connected finite etale covers inherit a unique generalized elliptic curve structure; negation extends to the whole curve
nodes.statement: (DR II Prop. 1.17) Let X/S be a generalized elliptic curve with unit e, and u : Y -> X a finite etale cover with a section e' in Y(S) over e such that the geometric fibres of Y/S are connected. Then Y has a unique generalized elliptic curve structure with unit e' compatible with + on X via u. (DR II Cor. 2.8) For any generalized elliptic curve C/S the inversion x -> -x on C^reg extends uniquely to an automorphism of C/S. (DR II 1.18) Multiplication by n on C^reg is flat with flat kernel C_n; over an algebraically closed field C_n has rank n^2 if C is smooth and rank n.(n,m) if C is an m-gon.

nodes.title: Contraction of a stable genus-one curve away from a finite locally free divisor in the smooth locus, and of generalized elliptic curves away from a subgroup
nodes.statement: Let p : C -> S be a stable genus-one curve and H c C^reg a closed subscheme finite locally free over S with non-empty fibres (automatically a relative Cartier divisor). There is a unique S-scheme C-bar with u : C -> C-bar such that C-bar is a stable genus-one curve and on every geometric fibre C-bar_s is obtained from C_s by contracting to a point each irreducible component not meeting H_s (DR IV Prop. 1.2); it is Proj of the graded algebra of p_* O(nH), its formation commutes with base change, u^{-1}(C-bar^sm) -> C-bar^sm is an isomorphism, the contraction is uniquely functorial for isomorphisms preserving H, and H is S-ample on C-bar. If C is a generalized elliptic curve and H = G is a finite locally free subgroup of C^sm, C-bar = c_G(C) has a unique generalized elliptic curve structure making u a homomorphism on u^{-1}(C-bar^sm) and equivariant, G becomes an ample subgroup of c_G(C)^sm, and c_G(C) = c_{G'}(C) canonically whenever G and G' meet the same components (DR IV 1.3-1.4; Conrad p. 7; Cesnavicius 3.2.1). In particular c(C) = contraction away from the identity section has geometrically irreducible fibres (DR IV Ex. 1.4).
hypotheses: C -> S stable genus-one curve; H c C^reg finite locally free over S with non-empty fibres

For DR IV 1.3: C a generalized elliptic curve whose geometric fibres are smooth or nm-gons; C-bar has smooth or n-gon fibres and is obtained by contracting the irreducible components of C_s that are closures of those connected components of C_s^reg whose order in pi_0(C_s^reg) does not divide n; fppf-locally on S a suitable H exists (take H = C_n, finite locally free by DR II 1.20)
proofSteps: Reduce to S noetherian; fibrewise H^0(C_s, O(-nH_s)) = 0 for n > 0, so by duality H^1(C_s, O(nH_s)) = 0 and by EGA III 7.8 the p_* O(nH) are locally free with base change (also n = 0 by II 1.6) (DR IV p. 205).

On irreducible fibres O(H_s) is ample; on polygons the contracted polygon receives O(nH_s) ample; the graded algebra is of finite type and its Proj C-bar is proper flat with base change; u satisfies (a),(b) (DR IV p. 206).
Uniqueness: u induces u^{-1}(C-bar^reg) = C-bar^reg fibrewise (EGA IV 17.8.2) and the graded algebras agree (DR IV p. 206).
Group structure: u^{-1}(C^reg-bar) acts on C-bar by transport of structure (DR IV 1.3); uniqueness of contractions gives functoriality for automorphisms (Conrad p. 7).
acceptance: Contracting the standard nm-gon with respect to its n-torsion gives the standard n-gon (Cesnavicius proof of Thm. 3.2.4(a)).
omega_{E/S} is canonically unchanged by contraction away from a finite subgroup, since u is an isomorphism near the identity sections (Conrad Section 4.4, p. 42).

nodes.title: Quotient E/G by an arbitrary finite locally free subgroup of E^sm, isogenies, and the isogeny-or-zero dichotomy
nodes.statement: Let E -> S be a generalized elliptic curve and G c E^sm an S-subgroup scheme finite locally free over S. The categorical quotient q : E -> E/G (initial among G-invariant S-morphisms) satisfies: (i) its formation commutes with arbitrary base change and E/G is S-flat; (ii) q is surjective, finite and universally open; (iii) E/G has a unique generalized elliptic curve structure making q a homomorphism, and E^sm/G (fppf quotient) = (E/G)^sm, so E^sm -> (E/G)^sm is finite locally free; (iv) for elliptic E, q is the isogeny with kernel G (Cesnavicius Thm. 2.2.4). E -> E/G is initial among homomorphisms killing G; a surjective homomorphism f has finite locally free kernel in E^sm and E/Ker f = E'; quotients may be taken in stages (Cor. 2.2.7). An isogeny is a surjective homomorphism, of degree the order of its kernel (Def. 2.2.8); every homomorphism is Zariski-locally an isogeny or zero (Prop. 2.2.9), and an isogeny maps E^sing into E'^sing (Prop. 2.2.10). Unlike isogenies of elliptic curves, E -> E/mu_d is not flat at singular points for d > 1 (Remark 2.2.3). Conrad's earlier restricted version requires G to meet the identity components of non-smooth fibres trivially, in which case G acts freely and E/G is the fppf quotient (Conrad Example 2.1.6).
hypotheses: E -> S a generalized elliptic curve over an arbitrary scheme S
G c E^sm a finite locally free S-subgroup (no etaleness or intersection condition in Cesnavicius's version)
proofSteps: Zariski-locally E is projective, so E is covered by G-invariant affines and q is glued from rings of invariants (SGA 3 I new V 4.1); on E^sm the action is free so E^sm/G is the fppf quotient (Cesnavicius p. 11).

(i): reduce to R noetherian and I-adically complete for I cutting out S^infinity; algebraize the subgroups G intersect (E^sm)^0 mod I^j to H c (E^sm)^0 of multiplicative type (Grothendieck existence [Ill05 8.4.5, 8.4.7]); after a finite locally free cover H is diagonalizable, so invariants commute with base change (SGA 3 I 4.7.3); G/H acts freely on E/H.
(ii): q integral hence finite (SGA 3 V 4.1(ii)); universally open by [Ryd13, 2.4].

(iii): E/G -> S is proper flat of finite presentation; on geometric fibres E/G is an elliptic curve or, via Example 2.2.1 (E -> E/mu_d induced by d-th powers on each P^1), the standard n-gon with n = N/#(G/H); the action extends by comparing E^sm/G x E/G with (E^sm x E)/(G x G); Pic^0-triviality follows fibrewise (Remark 2.1.4).
Prop. 2.2.9 from [MFK94, Prop. 6.1] after reduction to a noetherian base; Prop. 2.2.10 by reducing to Ker f c G_m (the maps f_d) or Ker f intersect G_m = 0 (etale, Fitting ideals SGA 7 VI 5.1).
acceptance: Example 2.2.1: for the standard n-gon over Z, E/mu_d is again the standard n-gon and q is induced by d-th powers; its formation commutes with arbitrary base change.

Remark 2.2.3: for d > 1 the homomorphism E -> E/mu_d of Example 2.2.1 (standard n-gon) is not flat at the singular points, by the formal criterion of flatness [BouAC III Sec. 5 no. 2 Thm 1]; the source makes this claim only for this example (flatness of more general isogenies of degenerate curves is not asserted either way).

nodes.title: Algebraization of formal generalized elliptic curves with a fixed number of degenerate components
nodes.statement: Let A be an adic noetherian ring with ideal of definition I and A_n = A/I^{n+1}. Reduction E -> (E mod I^{n+1})_n is an equivalence between generalized elliptic curves over Spec A whose degenerate geometric fibres all have a common number of irreducible components and compatible systems (E_n) of such generalized elliptic curves over the Spec A_n (Conrad Cor. 2.2.4). The content is that E^sm is not proper over the base, so formal GAGA does not apply directly to the group law.
hypotheses: A adic noetherian with ideal of definition I
a fixed number d of irreducible components on all degenerate geometric fibres (automatic when Spec A is local, by DR II 1.15)
proofSteps: D_n = E_n^sm[d] is quasi-finite, separated, flat of constant fibral rank d^2, hence finite over Spec A_n by DR II 1.19; so D_n c E_n is a relatively ample relative effective Cartier divisor.

Grothendieck's formal GAGA and existence theorems (EGA III_1 5.4.1, 5.4.5) give a proper flat A-scheme E, a finite flat d-torsion group D c E and an action D x E -> E lifting the data; D lies in E^sm because the only open of Spec A containing Spec A/I is Spec A.

E is a stable genus-one curve by openness (Conrad Lemma 2.1.3); D acts trivially on Pic^0 over Spec A/I, hence everywhere by Cor. 2.2.3, giving the unique generalized elliptic curve structure; D = E^sm[d] by orders; functoriality gives a quasi-inverse.
acceptance: Tate_n: the formal n-gon Tate curve over Spf Z[[q^{1/n}]] algebraizes uniquely to a generalized elliptic curve over Spec Z[[q^{1/n}]] (Conrad Section 2.5, used in R13.3).
Cesnavicius Thm. 3.4.2(a) reproves this via formal GAGA for proper stacks with finite diagonal (Lemma 3.4.1, [Ols06, A.1]) once the stacks Ell_n are available (R13.2).

nodes.title: Ampleness of level divisors: O(rD) ample with vanishing R^1, tri-canonical embedding, projectivity and fpqc descent
nodes.statement: A finite locally free subgroup G c E^sm of a generalized elliptic curve E -> S is ample if it is S-ample as a relative effective Cartier divisor on E, equivalently if it meets every irreducible component of every geometric fibre; a Drinfeld A-structure alpha is ample if its divisor D_alpha is (Cesnavicius Def. 4.2.13; Conrad Defs 2.4.1-2.4.3 impose the same condition on level structures). More generally, for a stable genus-one curve f : C -> S and a relative effective Cartier divisor D of degree d >= 1 supported in C^sm and meeting all irreducible components of all geometric fibres: for r >= 1, O(rD) is S-ample, R^1 f_* O(rD) = 0, f_* O(rD) is locally free of rank rd with formation compatible with base change, and for r >= 3 the map f^* f_* O(rD) -> O(rD) is surjective and C = Proj(sum_{n>=0} f_* O(nD)) -> P(f_* O(rD)) is a closed immersion (Conrad Lemma 2.4.7). Consequences: by DR II 1.15, II 1.20 and KM 1.2.3, over the open S minus the union of the S^{infinity,pi,n} with n != n', the n'-torsion E^sm[n'] is a pi-ample relative effective Cartier divisor, so every generalized elliptic curve is Zariski-locally projective over S (Cesnavicius Remark 2.1.9); ampleness provides the canonical S-ample line bundle O_E(D) that makes descent data effective, so moduli of ample level structures, and Ell_n via E^sm[n], are fpqc stacks (Conrad p. 16; Cesnavicius Remarks 3.1.2, 4.2.14); if alpha is ample and S is a geometric point, only the identity automorphism of (E, alpha) fixes (E^sm)^0 (Cesnavicius Remark 4.2.14 via Lemma 2.1.6).
hypotheses: f : C -> S stable genus-one curve; D relative effective Cartier divisor of degree d >= 1 supported in C^sm meeting all components of all geometric fibres
r >= 3 for the closed immersion
proofSteps: Conrad (p. 16) says only that the proof 'goes as in the higher-genus case in [DM, 1.2]'. DM Thm 1.2 (Publ. IHES 36, 1969, read by the reviewer in the public Numdam copy) proves, for a stable curve of genus g >= 2 over an algebraically closed field, H^1(C, omega^{n}) = 0 for n >= 2 and omega^{n} very ample for n >= 3, via positivity of the degree on every component, duality, and the criterion H^1(C, m_x m_y L) = 0 checked separately at smooth and double points. The genus-one adaptation (O(rD) in place of omega^{n}, using omega_{C_s} = O_{C_s} and deg O(D)|_E >= 1 on every component E) and the passage to the relative statement by cohomology and base change are written in neither source.
Ampleness can be tested on geometric fibres (EGA IV_3 9.6.4), giving the openness of the ample locus used in the representability arguments (Cesnavicius proof of Prop. 4.2.15).
acceptance: A Gamma(N)-structure forces all singular geometric fibres to be N-gons; a Gamma_1(N)-structure forces d-gons with d | N (Conrad p. 14, after Defs 2.4.1-2.4.2).
On the standard 2-gon in characteristic 2 an ample Z/NZ-structure through (1,1) has trivial infinitesimal automorphisms (Conrad Lemma 3.1.8 proof).

nodes.title: Tate curves with n sides: Raynaud's formal gluing over Z[[q^{1/n}]], algebraization, degeneracy locus (q^{1/n}), n-torsion mu_n x Z/nZ and formal group G_m-hat
nodes.statement: For n > 1 and i in Z/nZ let Delta_i = Spf Z[[q^{1/n}]]{{X_i, Y_i}}/(X_i Y_i - q^{1/n}), with opens Delta_i^+ = Delta_i{1/X_i}, Delta_i^- = Delta_i{1/Y_i}; gluing Delta_i^- to Delta_{i+1}^+ via Y_i = X_{i+1}, X_i = Y_{i+1} gives the formal n-gon Tate curve over Spf Z[[q^{1/n}]], flat and proper with reduction mod q^{1/n} the standard n-gon over Z, with Z/nZ embedded by i -> (1, q^{1/n}) in Delta_i and a formal rotation action (2.5.1) lifting the rotation of the standard n-gon. For m | n, m > 1, the map Tate_n(q^{1/m}) -> Tate_m is the finite etale quotient by the formally free action of mZ/nZ, and the quotient of Tate_n(q) by Z/nZ is a proper flat formal curve over Spf Z[[q]] with standard 1-gon reduction mod q, canonically independent of n > 1: the formal 1-gon Tate curve. By the construction principle each infinitesimal neighbourhood carries a unique generalized elliptic curve structure compatible with the action of the ample divisor Z/nZ, and by algebraization this gives a unique generalized elliptic curve Tate_n -> Spec Z[[q^{1/n}]], smooth away from q^{1/n} = 0 with locus of non-smoothness the zero scheme of q^{1/n}; there are unique isomorphisms Tate_n^sm[n] = mu_n x Z/nZ (2.5.2) and (Tate_n)^_0 = G_m-hat (2.5.3) lifting the canonical ones mod q^{1/n}. For m, n >= 1 there is a unique degree-m finite flat map of pointed formal curves pi_m : Tate_n(t) -> Tate_n(t^m) over Spf Z[[t]] inducing the m-th power on G_m-hat with pi_m^{-1}(1) = mu_m (X_i -> X_i^m, Y_i -> Y_i^m); over t != 0 its algebraization is an m-isogeny with kernel the lift of mu_m (Conrad Example 2.5.1). DR VII 1 constructs Tate curves G~_m^t/g^Z by Raynaud's method (Conrad: 'cf. [DR, VII]'): for t nilpotent and g a section of T_k c G_m^t with k != 0, (G~_m^t/g^Z, +) is a generalized elliptic curve with k-gon geometric fibres (Prop. 1.9); for A noetherian and t-adically complete the resulting formal generalized elliptic curve is algebraizable (1.10); the non-smooth locus has equation t = 0 (Prop. 1.11); Tate curves carry a canonical invariant differential dx/x (1.12); the k-torsion is an extension of Z/k by mu_k (1.13); the Tate curve with k sides is the contraction of the one with km sides (Construction 1.14); Def. 1.16 defines the Tate curve with k sides over Z[[q^{1/k}]] as G~_m^{q^{1/k}}/q^Z, with the structures (1.16.1) C^ = G_m^, (1.16.2) dx/x, (1.16.3) mu_n -> C_n and (1.16.4) C_k = mu_k x Z/k, and records that for one of the two natural definitions of e_k-products one has, via (1.16.4), e_n((a,b),(c,d)) = a.d - b.c (as printed).
hypotheses: n > 1 for the gluing (n = 1 by the quotient); base Z[[q^{1/n}]] or, by base change, any adic noetherian R with a topologically nilpotent r in place of q^{1/n}
Uniqueness of (2.5.3): the identity of G_m-hat over a noetherian ring has no non-trivial infinitesimal deformations when all maximal ideals have positive residue characteristic
DR VII 1.10: A noetherian and t-adically complete
proofSteps: Glue the formal annuli; the reduction mod q^{1/n} is the standard n-gon, so the formal curve is proper; flatness by construction (Conrad p. 17).
Apply Conrad Cor. 2.2.3 to the rotation action of the ample divisor Z/nZ on each infinitesimal neighbourhood, then Cor. 2.2.4 to algebraize (Conrad p. 17).
Formal Fitting-ideal computation on the Delta_i gives the non-smooth locus (q^{1/n}); (2.5.2) lifts the canonical isomorphism on the n-gon fibre.
(2.5.3): the open subgroup Delta_0^+{1/X_0} = Spf Z[[q^{1/n}]]{{X_0, 1/X_0}} has completion G_m-hat along X_0 = 1; uniqueness by rigidity of G_m-hat (Conrad pp. 17-18).
Example 2.5.1: define pi_m on annuli by m-th powers (after passing to a quotient when n = 1).

DR route (VII 1.10, p. 295): the formal curve is algebraizable by Grothendieck's existence theorem; for k = 1 the law + is determined by the neutral section (II 2.7); in general an fppf descent reduces to g = g_0^k, where G~_m^t/g^Z is a covering of G~_m^t/g_0^Z and II 1.17 applies (DR attribute the argument to 'la demonstration de III 1.2'). The non-smooth-locus computation of 1.11 is 'laisse au lecteur' for G~_m^t (as Conrad's 'formal Fitting-ideal calculation' is not written out either); it reduces to the chart xy = t, whose singular locus (x, y) has image V(t) (compare Conrad Example 2.1.7).

nodes.title: Tate_1 over W[[q]] is the algebraized universal deformation of the standard 1-gon
nodes.statement:
Let k be an algebraically closed field with Cohen ring W. By DR III Thm 1.2 (hypothesis: C_0 smooth or the standard n-gon with n prime to the characteristic exponent of k, which holds for the standard 1-gon in every characteristic), the deformation functor of the standard 1-gon over k as a generalized elliptic curve has no non-zero infinitesimal automorphisms and is pro-represented by a curve over Spec W[[t]], where t = 0 can be chosen to be the image of the non-smooth locus (DR III 1.2(i)-(iv), proved for irreducible C_0 in 1.3). Conrad: this deformation theory is formally smooth on one parameter [DR III 1.2(iii)] and is pro-represented by the formal Tate curve over W[[q]], which is a non-trivial deformation over k[q]/(q^2) because its non-smoothness locus is Spec k (q = 0; Example 2.1.9); by Cor. 2.2.4, Tate_1 -> Spec W[[q]] is the unique algebraization of the universal formal deformation (Conrad Lemma 3.3.5). Consequently, for every artin local W-algebra R with residue field k and every deformation E' of the standard 1-gon over R, there are a unique local W-algebra map W[[q]] -> R and a unique isomorphism E' = Tate_1 tensor_{W[[q]]} R lifting the identification of the closed fibre with the standard 1-gon; it is compatible with the canonical identifications of the N-torsion of the smooth loci with mu_N (Conrad (3.3.3), stated there for E' = E/

). Globally, DR VII Thm 2.1 states that the morphism Spec Z[[q]] -> M_1 defined by the Tate curve over Z[[q]] identifies Z[[q]] with the formal completion of M_1 along the section at infinity f_1; Cesnavicius (proof of Prop. 2.2.11) restates this as: Tate_1 realizes Spec Z[[q]] as an etale double cover of the formal completion of Ell_1 along Ell_1^infinity.
hypotheses: k algebraically closed, W a Cohen ring for k; deformations over artin (or complete noetherian) local W-algebras with residue field k

DR III 1.2 hypothesis: C_0 smooth, or the standard n-gon with n prime to the characteristic exponent p of k (DR III 1.1-1.2, p. 197, page image checked); for the standard 1-gon (n = 1) it holds in every characteristic
proofSteps: DR III 1.2 for irreducible C_0 (1.3, pp. 198-199): by II 2.7 the deformations of (C_0, +) are those of the pointed curve (C_0, e); the functor is pro-representable (a formal curve is projective, hence algebraizable) and formally smooth of relative dimension one since dim Ext^1(Omega^1_{C_0}(e), O) = 1 and Ext^2 = 0 (duality I 2.2 with omega_{C_0} = O; for the 1-gon via the normalization P^1); (iv) from the deformation theory of ordinary double points and II 1.15. (i) follows from II 1.10 and pro-representability from (i) and [25].
The formal Tate curve over W[[q]] is a non-trivial first-order deformation since its degeneracy locus is q = 0 (Conrad Example 2.1.9 type computation), hence pro-represents the functor.
Algebraize by Conrad Cor. 2.2.4; the isomorphism (3.3.3) respects the identifications with mu_N because Aut(mu_N) is etale.

DR VII 2.1 proof (pp. 298-299): M_1 is smooth over Z, so its formal completion along f_1 is Spf Z[[t]] and tau is q -> t = f(q); the image of the non-smooth locus of the universal curve is f_1 (IV 2.2) and that of the Tate curve is q = 0 (VII 1.11); compatibility of this image with base change gives (q) = (f(q)), so tau is an isomorphism.
acceptance: The degree 2 in Cesnavicius's double-cover formulation of DR VII 2.1 matches Aut(standard 1-gon) = Z/2Z (Conrad Example 2.1.5, DR II 1.10); DR's own statement identifies Z[[q]] with the completion of M_1 along the section f_1, so any formal statement must fix which formulation (section or boundary substack) is meant.
The pullback of Tate_1 along W[[q]] -> k[q]/(q^2) is a non-trivial first-order deformation: its degeneracy locus is the closed point q = 0, not all of Spec k[q]/(q^2).

nodes.title: Isom-schemes of generalized elliptic curves: quasi-finite in general, finite when degenerate polygon sizes match, finite for Gamma-structures
nodes.statement: For generalized elliptic curves E, E' over S, Isom(E,E') is represented by a quasi-finite separated finitely presented (hence quasi-affine) S-scheme (Conrad Thm 3.1.2). If the loci of n-gon and n'-gon degenerate fibres are disjoint for n != n', Isom(E,E') is S-finite, and for S normal (Cesnavicius: integral normal) with dense open S*, isomorphisms over S* extend uniquely (Conrad Thm 3.2.4; Cesnavicius Prop. 3.1.8 with Lemma 3.1.9). For Gamma in {Gamma(N), Gamma_1(N;n)} the Isom-schemes of Gamma-structures are finite, so M_Gamma is separated and isomorphisms over a dense open of a normal base extend (Conrad Thm 3.2.2); for a reduced effective Cartier divisor D c S, isomorphisms over S - D extend uniquely over S (Conrad Cors 3.2.3 and 3.2.5, since R is integrally closed in R[1/r] when R/(r) is reduced).
hypotheses: E, E' generalized elliptic curves over a scheme S
Finiteness: no geometric point where E and E' are degenerate with different numbers of components
Extension: S normal and S* dense open (Conrad); S integral normal (Cesnavicius 3.1.8(b)); or S - D with D a reduced effective Cartier divisor
proofSteps: Thm 3.1.2: away from the degeneracy loci Isom is finite by Hilbert schemes and the valuative criterion; near S^infinity work fpqc-locally where E^sm[n] is a split extension of Z/nZ by mu_n, parametrize the etale ample subgroups H' of E'^sm[n] by a quasi-finite S', and reduce to the irreducible-fibre quotients E/H, E'/H' where the proof of DR III 2.5 applies.

Thm 3.2.2: check the valuative criterion over a complete DVR R with algebraically closed residue field, allowing a finite flat DVR extension by descent. Generically degenerate: Lemma 3.2.1 (standard d-gon after finite flat base change, via Cor. 3.1.3) and finiteness of Aut(C_d). Generically smooth: make the level divisor D_K a sum of K-points; E_1, E_2 are normal (semistable curves are CM; Serre's criterion); successive blow-ups of each E_i at non-smooth points end at the minimal regular proper model E~ (adapting DM 1.12), and each E_i is the contraction of E~ away from the closure of D_K.

Thm 3.2.4: contract away from fibral identity components and apply Thm 3.2.2 for Gamma(1); use the open-closed finite mu c c(E)^sm[n], the exact sequence 0 -> mu -> E^sm[n] -> G -> 0 with G = Z/nZ, split after a finite extension, to produce Gamma_1(n)-structures P, P' and apply Thm 3.2.2 again; smooth closed fibres are handled by Neron models. Cesnavicius footnote 3 gives an alternative via BLR 7.4/3 and Zariski's main theorem.
Cor. 3.2.3/3.2.5: finiteness of Isom plus integral closedness of R in R[1/r] when R/(r) is reduced.
acceptance: Necessity of the disjointness hypothesis of Thm 3.2.4 (Conrad p. 24 says counterexamples are 'easy to construct' but writes none): over a complete DVR R with uniformizer pi, Tate_2(pi) (2-gon closed fibre) and Tate_1(pi^2) (1-gon closed fibre) have generic fibres identified by Conrad Thm 2.5.2, but this generic isomorphism does not extend over R, so Isom(Tate_1(pi^2), Tate_2(pi)) is not R-finite (reviewer's example).
Separatedness of M_Gamma(N) and M_Gamma_1(N;n) over Z.

nodes.title: M_Gamma is an Artin stack of finite type over Z: universal tri-canonically embedded Gamma-structures over a quasi-projective base
nodes.statement: For Gamma in {Gamma(N), Gamma_1(N;n)} (with ord_p(n) <= ord_p(N) for p | gcd(N,n)) the stack M_Gamma of Gamma-structures on generalized elliptic curves has diagonal representable by quasi-finite separated finitely presented maps of schemes (Conrad Lemma 3.1.1) and is an Artin stack of finite type over Spec Z (Thm 3.1.4). More precisely there is a universal generalized elliptic curve f_Gamma : E_Gamma -> S_Gamma with a Gamma-structure and a trivialization of f_Gamma* O(3 D_Gamma), D_Gamma the ample divisor generated by the structure, over a quasi-projective Z-scheme S_Gamma (Thm 3.1.6); S_Gamma -> M_Gamma is smooth and surjective.
hypotheses: Gamma = Gamma(N) (d = N^2) or Gamma_1(N;n) (d = Nn) with ord_p(n) <= ord_p(N) for all p | gcd(N,n) (Conrad Def. 2.4.3)
Artin stacks in the sense of [LMB] with Spec Z as base (Conrad 1.3)
proofSteps: Lemma 3.1.1: 'isomorphism carries one Gamma-structure to another' is a finitely presented closed condition [KM 1.3.5], so it reduces to Thm 3.1.2 (previous node).

Lemma 3.1.5: Hilbert schemes plus openness of the stable-genus-one locus (Lemma 2.1.3), of ampleness [EGA IV_3 9.6.4] and Lemma 2.4.7 give a universal (f, D, iota) over a quasi-projective H_0; a group structure on D is imposed by an affine finite type base change; quasi-compact Hom-schemes Hom(D_0, Isom(C_0,C_0)) (Hilbert polynomial 2dn + chi for graphs of automorphisms) give the action rho universally.
Triviality of the universal translation on Pic^0 is an open and closed condition (Lemma 2.2.1), and Cor. 2.2.3 then gives a universal generalized elliptic curve with ample subgroup D (3.1.2).

Thm 3.1.6: impose an A-generator of D universally by [KM 1.3.5] for Gamma(N); for Gamma_1(N;n) impose P in D[N], the subgroup condition [KM 1.3.7], a degree-n divisor C c D, subgroup condition, cyclicity via Thm 2.3.7 and Mumford's flattening stratification for C^x of rank phi(n), and the equalities of Cartier divisors (2.4.4) [KM 1.3.5]; Thm 2.4.5 identifies the result.
S_Gamma -> M_Gamma forgets the trivialization iota; its fibres parametrize trivializations of a rank-3d vector bundle, so it is smooth and surjective (Conrad calls it a projective-space bundle).
acceptance: For every N >= 1, over Z[1/N] a Gamma(N)-structure is an isomorphism (Z/NZ)^2 = E^sm[N] whose image meets every component ([KM 1.5.3], see Cesnavicius Remark 4.2.3), so M_Gamma(N)|Z[1/N] is Deligne-Rapoport's stack of level-N structures (DR IV 2); Conrad Remark 4.1.5 identifies M_Gamma(N) over Z with the normalization of M_1 in it. No restriction N >= 3 is needed.

Level one: Gamma(1)-structures are the identity section, whose divisor is S-ample exactly when all degenerate fibres are 1-gons, so the construction with d = 1 yields M_Gamma(1) = M_1 (Conrad uses Gamma = Gamma(1) in the proof of Thm 3.2.4, p. 25). Ampleness of D is what excludes n-gon fibres with n >= 2 from the universal family.

nodes.title: Deligne-Mumford loci: automorphism schemes of Gamma-structures over algebraically closed fields and the non-etale mu_p phenomenon at p^2 | n
nodes.statement:
Over an algebraically closed field k, Aut(E) and Aut(E, iota) are finite; Aut(E, iota) is etale if Gamma = Gamma(N), or if Gamma = Gamma_1(N;n) and, when char k = p > 0 and E is non-smooth, the p-part of C is etale or connected (automatic if p^2 does not divide n) (Conrad Lemma 3.1.8). Hence M_Gamma(N) is Deligne-Mumford, and M_Gamma_1(N;n) is Deligne-Mumford away from the open and closed part of M^infinity classifying degenerate triples in characteristic p whose p-part of C has geometric fibres that are non-etale and disconnected, in particular everywhere if n is squarefree (Thm 3.1.7); geometric points there have universal formal deformation rings with unique algebraizations (Cor. 3.1.9). The auxiliary stack of Gamma~_1(N;n)-structures (P, Q) is finite locally free of rank phi(n) over M_Gamma_1(N;n), finite etale of degree phi(n) after inverting n, and everywhere Deligne-Mumford (Def. 3.3.2 and the following paragraph, Lemma 3.3.3). Conrad's Thm 3.2.7 adds that M_Gamma_1(N;n) is Deligne-Mumford if and only if n is squarefree; the 'only if' is false. The excluded locus of Thm 3.1.7 is only a sufficient condition (the proof of Lemma 3.1.8 shows Aut(E; P, C) is etale whenever

is ample), and Cesnavicius Prop. 4.6.5(b), applied to X_1(N;n), which agrees with M_Gamma_1(N;n) (Cesnavicius p. 44), shows that M_Gamma_1(N;n) is Deligne-Mumford whenever ord_p(n) <= ord_p(N) + 1 for every prime p. Under Conrad's standing condition ord_p(n) <= ord_p(N) for p | gcd(N,n), M_Gamma_1(N;n) is therefore Deligne-Mumford if every prime p with p^2 | n divides N, and Cesnavicius (p. 44) states that it is not Deligne-Mumford in characteristics p not dividing N with p^2 | n. For example M_Gamma_1(p^2;p^2) is Deligne-Mumford although p^2 | n.
hypotheses: Gamma in {Gamma(N), Gamma_1(N;n)} with Conrad's condition ord_p(n) <= ord_p(N) for p | gcd(N,n)
DM criterion: an Artin stack is Deligne-Mumford iff its diagonal is formally unramified [LMB 8.1]; checked on geometric fibres
proofSteps: Aut-schemes are quasi-finite by Thm 3.1.2; etaleness means no non-trivial infinitesimal deformation of the identity.
Irreducible E: Aut(E) is etale ([Mum2, Cor. 6.2] for smooth E, Example 2.1.5 for the 1-gon).

d-gons with d >= 2: reduce Gamma_1(N;n) to Gamma_1(M) cases (constant prime-to-p parts; replace n by its p-part; etale C of order p^e lies on distinct components) and then show an ample Z/NZ-structure on the standard d-gon has no infinitesimal automorphisms (Example 2.1.5; the only exceptional case d = 2, P = (x,1), x^2 in mu_2, is handled separately in characteristic 2).
Lemma 3.3.3: for Gamma~_1-structures, shift l-parts of <Q> into P and reduce to Gamma_1(N_0 p^e) automorphism functors, which are etale.
acceptance: Over F_p with p^2 | n there is a Gamma_0(n)-type structure on a standard polygon with mu_p in its automorphism scheme (Conrad 1.1; Cesnavicius 1.2), so a Deligne-Mumford statement must exclude such points.
Characteristic 2 check: for the standard 2-gon and P = (1,1), mu_2 does not fix P (Conrad proof of Lemma 3.1.8).

Reviewer's check of the corrected criterion: on the standard p^2-gon E over F_p-bar take P = (1,1) and C = mu_p x <(1,p)>. Then (P, C) is a Gamma_1(p^2;p^2)-structure (the divisor sum over j of (jP + C) is p.(mu_p x Z/p^2Z) = mu_{p^2} x Z/p^2Z = E^sm[p^2], since p.[mu_p] = [mu_{p^2}] in characteristic p), C is neither etale nor connected, and the only point of mu_{p^2} c Aut(E) fixing P is 1, so Aut(E; P, C) is etale: this point lies in Conrad's excluded locus but the stack is Deligne-Mumford there.

nodes.title: Properness of M_Gamma over Z via genus-one stable reduction, schematic closure of the level divisor and contraction
nodes.statement: Let R be a complete DVR with fraction field K and (E_K, iota_K) a generalized elliptic curve with Gamma-structure over K. After base change to some DVR R' finite flat over R it extends to a Gamma-structure over R' (Conrad Lemma 3.2.6). Hence M_Gamma is proper over Z; M_Gamma(N) is Deligne-Mumford and smooth over Z[1/N], and M_Gamma_1(N;n) is smooth over Z[1/Nn] (Conrad Thm 3.2.7). For smoothness away from the level Conrad cites '[DR, III, 2.5(iii)]', but DR III Thm 2.5 has only parts (i) and (ii); (i) is the smoothness over Z of the stack M_* of generalized elliptic curves whose numbers of components are prime to the residue characteristics, which is presumably the intended input.
hypotheses: Gamma in {Gamma(N), Gamma_1(N;n)} (for Gamma_1(N;n) with Conrad's condition ord_p(n) <= ord_p(N) for p | gcd(N,n))
valuative criterion with DVRs suffices for locally noetherian Artin stacks ([O], [LMB 7.12])

DR IV 1.5-1.6 are stated for S the spectrum of a complete discrete valuation ring with algebraically closed residue field; Conrad applies 1.6(i),(ii) in Lemma 3.2.6 to an arbitrary complete DVR R and does not record the reduction to that case
proofSteps: M_Gamma is separated (Thm 3.2.2) and of finite type over Z (Thm 3.1.4), so properness reduces to the valuative criterion over DVRs (Conrad p. 25).

E_K not smooth: after finite base change E_K is the standard d-gon; the schematic closure of the level subgroup in the standard d-gon over R lies in E^sm (as E^sm[M] is finite flat) and is an ample subgroup.

E_K smooth: take the minimal regular proper model E; E_K(K) = E^sm(R); by the genus-one stable reduction theorem [DR IV 1.6(i),(ii)] after finite base change E is a generalized elliptic curve extending E_K; close up the level divisor (a sum of R-points in E^sm).
Restore ampleness by contracting the closed fibre along components disjoint from the level subgroup (R13.1 contraction) and transporting the structure through c^{-1}(Ebar^sm) = Ebar^sm.
acceptance: Reviewer's test of the smooth case: let R be a complete DVR with uniformizer pi, R' = R[pi^{1/p}], K' its fraction field. The Gamma_1(p)-structure on Tate_1(pi) over K' given by the section pi^{1/p} of G_m/pi^Z does not extend to Tate_1(pi) over R' (a 1-gon, into whose smooth locus the section does not specialize), but it extends as an ample Gamma_1(p)-structure on Tate_p(pi^{1/p}) over R' (a p-gon, the minimal regular model; its generic fibre is Tate_1(pi) by Conrad Thm 2.5.2), meeting every component, so no contraction is needed.

nodes.title: M_Gamma -> Spec Z is flat and CM of pure relative dimension 1 (Conrad's deformation-ring computation at the cusps)
nodes.statement: The proper morphism M_Gamma -> Spec Z is flat and Cohen-Macaulay with pure relative dimension 1 (Conrad Thm 3.3.1). The elliptic-curve locus M^0_Gamma is regular and Z-flat with fibres of pure dimension 1 (Lemma 3.3.4). At a Gamma(N)-structure (P_0,Q_0) on the standard N-gon over an algebraically closed k (Cohen ring W), the universal deformation ring is a local factor ring of the fppf mu_N-torsor (v^univ)^{-1}(1) tensor W[zeta_N][[q]] over W[zeta_N][[q]] (Lemma 3.3.6), hence finite flat over W[[q]]; the Gamma_1(N) and Gamma~_1(N;n) cases reduce to it (the latter giving the coordinate ring of mu^x_{p^r} over W[[t]] in the non-ample case).
hypotheses: Gamma in {Gamma(N), Gamma_1(N;n)}; for Gamma_1(N;n) work on the Deligne-Mumford finite locally free cover M_{Gamma~_1(N;n)}
k algebraically closed, W a Cohen ring for k
proofSteps: Lemma 3.3.4: Gamma_1(N), Gamma(N) are [KM 5.1.1]; Gamma~_1(N;n) reduces etale-locally to Gamma~_1(p^r;p^e) and to supersingular deformation rings whose maximal ideal is generated by two formal-group coordinates X(P), X(Q) as in [KM 5.3.2], via [KM 5.2.1, 5.2.2].

CM with fixed relative dimension is open and F_p-points are dense in finite type Z-stacks, so it suffices to show deformation rings of Gamma-structures on standard polygons over F_p-bar are 2-dimensional, W-flat and CM, i.e. have finite faithfully flat covers finite flat over W[[x]].

Gamma(N): lift the canonical sequence 0 -> mu_N -> E_0^sm[N] -> Z/NZ -> 0; E/

is a deformation of the 1-gon, pro-represented by Tate_1 over W[[q]] (R13.1 Tate node, Lemma 3.3.5); the unique etale isogeny E_N -> Tate_1 lifting C_N -> C_1 (DR II 1.17) gives (3.3.5), and choosing P amounts to a section of (v^univ)^{-1}(1).

Gamma_1(N): (v^univ)^{-1}(1) is an fppf mu_d-torsor over mu^x_{N/d} on Gamma_1(d)-deformation rings (Cor. 2.3.3); Drinfeld bases are finite locally free surjective over Z/NZ-structures ([KM 1.10.6, 8.10.7, 5.5.3]).

Gamma~_1(N;n): in the ample case B = A[T]/(Phi_{p^e}(T)); otherwise the etale Gamma_1(M p^e) part has deformation ring W[[t]] (DR II 1.17) and the answer is the coordinate ring of mu^x_{p^r} over W[[t]], regular of dimension 2.
acceptance: At the standard N-gon with Gamma(N)-structure, the local factor rings of (3.3.6) are finite flat over W[[q]] and correspond to choices of P_0 in v_0^{-1}(1)(k) and Q_0 in mu_N^x(k).
Cesnavicius (Thms 4.3.5, 4.4.4) reaches flatness and regularity of X(n), X_1(n) without deformation rings, by congruences with elliptic curves; the two routes must give the same stacks.

nodes.title: Contraction c_Gamma : M_Gamma -> M_1 is finite flat, M^infinity_Gamma is a relative Cartier divisor, M_Gamma is normal, and equals the Deligne-Rapoport normalization
nodes.statement: (Conrad Thm 4.1.1(1), Lemmas 4.1.2-4.1.4, Remark 4.1.5, Lemma 4.2.3) For Gamma(N), the contraction c_Gamma : M_Gamma -> M_1 is relatively representable, finite and faithfully flat; for Gamma_1(N;n) the same holds over M_1^0 and over M_1 when n is squarefree. M^infinity_Gamma c M_Gamma is a relative effective Cartier divisor over Spec Z for all Gamma. M_Gamma is normal, and regular away from the part of M^infinity_Gamma in characteristics dividing the level (full regularity, Thm 4.1.1(2), is decomposed at R13.3). Consequently (n squarefree for Gamma_1(N;n)) M_Gamma is canonically the normalization of M_1 in the finite flat Deligne-Mumford stack M_Gamma|Z[1/level], i.e. the Deligne-Rapoport compactification (Remark 4.1.5). Remark 4.1.5 adds that for non-squarefree n this normalization cannot recover M_Gamma_1(N;n) because that stack is not Deligne-Mumford along M^infinity in characteristic p when p^2 | n. That is so only when some prime p with p^2 | n does not divide N: if every such p divides N, then M_Gamma_1(N;n) = X_1(N;n) is Deligne-Mumford with representable contraction to X(1) and equals the normalization X_Gamma1(N;n) (Cesnavicius p. 44, Prop. 4.6.5(b), Thm 4.6.6(b)). The contractions M_Gamma(N) -> M_Gamma_1(N), M_Gamma(N) -> M_Gamma(d), M_Gamma_1(N) -> M_Gamma_1(d) (d | N), M_Gamma_1(N;n) -> M_Gamma_1(N) (n squarefree) and M_Gamma_1(N) -> M_Gamma_0(N) (Conrad's Gamma_0(N) = Gamma_1(1;N), the naive stack) are finite flat surjective of constant rank.
hypotheses: n squarefree (or restriction to M_1^0) for the Gamma_1(N;n) finiteness and normalization statements
Lemma 4.1.3: A -> B local map of local noetherian rings, A regular, B CM, dim B = dim A + dim B/m_A B implies B flat [CRT 23.1]
proofSteps: Cartier divisor: reduce Gamma_1(N;n) to the Gamma~ cover; for Gamma(N) identify E_N over W[[q]] with Tate_N(q) (4.1.2) by DR II 1.17, whose non-smooth locus is (q), and pull back along the faithfully flat W[[q]] -> (v^univ)^{-1}(1) tensor W[zeta_N][[q]].

Finiteness of c_Gamma: proper quasi-finite; representable by Cor. 2.2.7 and Thm 2.2.5(2) because no non-trivial automorphism of a Gamma-structure over k induces the identity on the contraction c(E) (Example 2.1.5; squarefree n used for the C-part).
Flatness: M_Gamma CM of relative dimension 1 (Thm 3.3.1), M_1 smooth, so Lemma 4.1.3 applies.

Normality: Serre's criterion on deformation rings; smooth over Q; regular off the Cartier divisor M^infinity by Lemma 3.3.4, which contains no codimension-one points of positive residue characteristic.
Remark 4.1.5: finite flat over regular M_1 plus normal gives the normalization identification.
Lemma 4.2.3: compare with the finite flat maps to M_1; flatness by Lemma 4.1.3; constant rank on the locus where the level is invertible; case (4) from Thm 2.3.7.
acceptance: Rank check over Z[1/N]: M_Gamma(N) -> M_1 has degree #GL_2(Z/NZ) and M_Gamma_1(N) -> M_Gamma_0(N) degree phi(N).

For n = p^2, c : M_Gamma_1(1;p^2) = M_Gamma_0(p^2) -> M_1 is not representable, hence not finite, at the p-gon cusps, already over C: the mu_p of automorphisms of the standard p-gon fixing G_m x {0} stabilizes <(zeta_{p^2}, 1)> and contracts to the identity (Cesnavicius 1.2). Over F_p these points moreover have non-etale automorphism group schemes.

nodes.title: The stacks Ell_n: algebraic with finite diagonal, proper and smooth over Z; Deligne-Mumford locus; boundary a reduced relative Cartier divisor
nodes.statement: For n >= 1 let Ell_n be the Z-stack of generalized elliptic curves whose degenerate geometric fibres are n-gons, and Ell_n^infinity the closed substack cut out by the degeneracy loci (well defined by base change compatibility of S^infinity). Then (a) Ell_n is algebraic with finite diagonal, proper, and smooth of relative dimension 1 over Z; (b) its largest Deligne-Mumford open substack is Ell_n minus (Ell_n^infinity) tensor Z/nZ, i.e. minus the boundary in characteristics dividing n; (c) Spec Z -> Ell_n^infinity given by the standard n-gon is surjective, representable and finite locally free of rank 2n, so Ell_n^infinity is irreducible with geometrically irreducible fibres and Z-smooth of relative dimension 0; (d) Ell_n^infinity c Ell_n is a reduced relative effective Cartier divisor over Spec Z (Cesnavicius Thm 3.1.6). Ell_1 is the compactification often written M_{1,1} bar, Deligne-Mumford, proper and smooth over Z (Cesnavicius 4.1.1 citing DR III 2.5, III 1.2(iii), IV 2.2).
hypotheses: n >= 1; base Spec Z (no level inverted)
B_n (DR V 1.3): pairs (E, G) with degenerate fibres n-gons and G c E^sm finite etale, etale-locally Z/nZ, meeting all components
proofSteps: Prop. 3.1.5(a): B_n is Deligne-Mumford and Z-smooth of relative dimension 1 by DR V 1.4.

Prop. 3.1.5(b): B_n -> Ell_n factors through the open Ell_n^{n-ord} (remove supersingular j in characteristics dividing n, via q(E) = E/E^sm[n] and j); representability, quasi-finiteness and flatness via the functor F_1 of points P in E^sm[n] giving closed immersions Z/nZ -> E^sm[n], an open subfunctor of E^sm[n].
Prop. 3.1.5(c): algebraicity and smoothness of Ell_n^{n-ord} from a smooth atlas of B_n ([SP 06DC], EGA IV_4 17.7.7).

Thm 3.1.6(a): Ell_n = Ell union Ell_n^{n-ord}; finite diagonal by Conrad 3.2.4 (previous node); quasi-compact since Ell and Spec Z (standard n-gon) cover; properness by the valuative criterion [LMB 7.10] from semistable reduction and contractions.

(b): Remark 3.1.7 (largest open with unramified automorphism functors, via Conrad 2.2.5(2)) and Lemma 2.1.6 (mu_n non-etale in characteristics dividing n); (c): Isom with the standard n-gon is finite locally free of rank 2n; (d): Ell_n regular, Ell_n^infinity smooth of codimension one on a smooth atlas, so Weil = Cartier.
acceptance: Ell_1 = M_{1,1}bar is Deligne-Mumford (n = 1: no characteristic excluded).
Over F_p with p | n the standard n-gon has automorphism group scheme mu_n x Z/2Z, non-etale: Ell_n is not Deligne-Mumford there.

nodes.title: The tower of compactifications: contractions Ell_nm -> Ell_n are proper flat surjective, degeneracy ideals multiply by m, and every generalized elliptic curve decontracts fppf-locally
nodes.statement: For n, m >= 1 the contraction c : Ell_nm -> Ell_n, E -> c_{E^sm[n]}(E), and c' : B_nm -> B_n are flat and of finite presentation; c is proper with finite diagonal and surjective; c' is representable by schemes, separated and quasi-finite (Cesnavicius Thm 3.2.4(a)). The pullback of Ell_n^infinity is the relative effective Cartier divisor m.[Ell_nm^infinity] (Thm 3.2.4(b),(c)); equivalently, if E has nm-gon degenerate fibres and E' is its contraction with respect to E^sm[n], the degeneracy ideals satisfy I_{S^infinity,E'} = (I_{S^infinity,E})^m (Cor. 3.2.5). Every generalized elliptic curve is, fppf-locally on S (by a locally quasi-finite cover), the contraction of one whose degenerate fibres have a number of components divisible by any given n (Cor. 3.2.6). Over R noetherian and complete for the ideal I of S^infinity: (E^sm)^0 has a unique finite locally free subgroup B_n of order n, etale-locally mu_n; if m divides n and the component numbers, E^sm[n] has a largest finite locally free subgroup A_{n,m} meeting exactly m components, of order nm, an extension of an etale-locally Z/mZ group C_m by B_n; over S - S^infinity, B_n sits in 0 -> B_n -> E[n] -> C'_n -> 0 with C'_n etale-locally Z/nZ (Prop. 3.2.7).
hypotheses: Prop. 3.2.7: S = Spec R, R noetherian, complete and separated for the ideal I cutting out S^infinity
proofSteps: (a): a, b (forgetting G) are representable, separated, quasi-finite, faithfully flat onto the n-ordinary loci (Prop. 3.1.5(b)); c' is representable by Lemma 3.2.2(b) and Lemma 2.1.6 (no non-identity automorphism of an ample (E,G) is trivial on (E^sm)^0), quasi-finite since there are finitely many subgroups of order nm, and flat as a quasi-finite map of smooth Deligne-Mumford stacks of relative dimension 1 (EGA IV_2 6.1.5); c is the identity on Ell, so its flatness follows from that of c'.
(b): c flat pulls back the relative Cartier divisor Ell_n^infinity; supports agree and Ell_nm^infinity is irreducible and reduced, so the pullback is a positive multiple.

(c): the multiple is computed on Tate curves, using DR VII 1.11 and 1.14 (degeneracy ideal of the Tate curve with k sides and contraction of Tate curves), i.e. the Tate-curve construction node of R13.1.
Cor. 3.2.6: flatness, surjectivity and finite presentation of Ell_nd -> Ell_d plus EGA IV_4 17.16.2.
Prop. 3.2.7: (a) on infinitesimal thickenings by Lemma 2.1.11, algebraized by EGA III_1 5.1.4, 5.4.1; (b) reduce to a complete DVR (EGA II 7.1.9) and decontract by Cor. 3.2.6.
acceptance: Tate check: contracting Tate_{km}(q^{1/km}) to Tate_k(q^{1/k}) multiplies the degeneracy ideal: (q^{1/k}) = (q^{1/km})^m.

For m > 1, c : Ell_nm -> Ell_n is not representable by algebraic spaces, even over C: on the standard nm-gon, zeta in mu_m c mu_nm c Aut(E) (Lemma 2.1.6) acts by zeta^{jm} = 1 on each component of index jm, i.e. on every component meeting E^sm[n], so it induces the identity on c_{E^sm[n]}(E) (criterion Lemma 3.2.2(b)). By contrast c' : B_nm -> B_n is representable by schemes (Thm 3.2.4(a)). (Reviewer's deduction; the source states only the properties of c in Thm 3.2.4(a).)

nodes.title: Deligne-Rapoport modular stacks X_H of congruence level H via normalization of X(1)
nodes.statement: For an open subgroup H of GL_2(Z-hat) choose n >= 1 with ker(GL_2(Z-hat) -> GL_2(Z/nZ)) c H and let H-bar be the image of H in GL_2(Z/nZ). Let Y_H[1/n] be the Z[1/n]-stack of elliptic curves E -> S with an S-point of the finite etale S-scheme H-bar \ Isom(E[n], (Z/nZ)^2). The modular stack X_H is the Deligne-Mumford X(1)-stack obtained by normalizing X(1) = Ell_1 with respect to the finite etale Y_H[1/n] -> Y(1)_Z[1/n]; Y_H is the preimage of Y(1). Different choices of n give canonically isomorphic X_H (DR IV 3.6). X_H -> X(1) is representable, finite, surjective and flat (EGA IV_2 6.1.5 via going down and normality), locally free of rank [GL_2(Z-hat) : H]; X_H is of relative dimension 1 over Z at every point and smooth over Z[1/n] (DR IV 6.7). For H' c H there is a finite X(1)-morphism X_H' -> X_H. An open substack of X_H whose geometric points have no non-trivial automorphisms is a quasi-projective Z-scheme (Lemma 4.1.3), and X_H has a unique largest open subscheme (Remark 4.1.4).
hypotheses: H open (finite index) in GL_2(Z-hat); n with Gamma(n) c H
X(1) = Ell_1 Deligne-Mumford, proper and smooth over Z (DR III 2.5(i), III 1.2(iii), IV 2.2)
proofSteps: Define Y_H[1/n] by the quotient of the finite etale Isom-scheme by H-bar (DR IV 3; Cesnavicius 4.1.2).
Normalize the regular stack X(1) in the finite etale Y_H[1/n] (DR IV 3.3); independence of n by DR IV 3.6.
Flatness: X_H normal of dimension 2, X(1) regular, finite map, so EGA IV_2 6.1.5 applies; rank read on Y.
Lemma 4.1.3: U is an algebraic space by Lemma 3.2.2(a), U -> P^1_Z separated quasi-finite (coarse j-map), hence a scheme (Lemma 3.2.3) and quasi-projective (EGA IV_3 8.11.2).
acceptance: For H = GL_2(Z-hat), X_H = X(1).
The problem this node leaves open, and which R13.2's modular descriptions solve, is a functor-of-points description of X_H over Z without inverting n.

nodes.title: Drinfeld A-structures, the Katz-Mazur cyclicity criterion and standard cyclic subgroups on generalized elliptic curves (via congruences with elliptic curves)
nodes.statement: For a generalized elliptic curve E -> S, a Drinfeld A-structure (A finite abelian) is a homomorphism alpha : A -> E^sm(S) whose divisor D_alpha = sum [alpha(a)] is a subgroup scheme (Cesnavicius Def. 4.2.2); G c E^sm finite locally free is cyclic of order n if fppf-locally it has a Drinfeld Z/nZ-structure (Def. 4.2.6; Conrad Def. 2.3.4). Key congruence lemma: if n divides the component numbers of degenerate fibres, fppf-locally there is an elliptic curve E' with E^sm[n] = E'[n] (Lemma 4.2.1). Consequences (each the generalized-elliptic analogue of Katz-Mazur): restrictions of Drinfeld structures to n-torsion (Prop. 4.2.5); G cyclic iff its scheme of generators G^x is finite locally free of rank phi(n) (Katz-Mazur cyclicity criterion; Conrad Thm 2.3.7), G^x = sum over units of [i.g], cyclicity is represented by a finitely presented closed subscheme, squarefree order implies cyclic (Conrad Cor. 2.3.8), and standard cyclic subgroups G_d are well defined (Prop. 4.2.7; Conrad Thm 2.3.5, Def. 2.3.6); standard cyclic subgroups and standard-order factorizations of cyclic isogenies (Props 4.2.9-4.2.10); for cyclic G, H of orders n, m with [G_d + H_d] = E^sm[d] (d = gcd) and d dividing the component numbers, [G + H] is a finite locally free subgroup of order nm killed by lcm(n,m) (Prop. 4.2.11(b), generalizing Conrad Thm 2.4.5); representability and ranks of the functors of Drinfeld structures and of pairs of cyclic subgroups (Props 4.2.12, 4.2.15).
hypotheses: E -> S generalized elliptic curve over an arbitrary scheme; statements needing E^sm[N] of rank N^2 assume N divides the number of components of each degenerate geometric fibre (removable fppf-locally by decontraction)
proofSteps: Lemma 4.2.1: reduce to S strictly henselian local with degenerate special fibre; E^sm[n] is an extension of Z/nZ by mu_n, split fppf-locally; lift an ordinary elliptic curve over the residue field and use its connected-etale sequence.

Reduction pattern: work fppf-locally; decontract via Cor. 3.2.6 so that n divides the component numbers; replace E^sm[n] by E'[n] (Lemma 4.2.1); by [KM 1.10.6] the properties depend only on the finite group scheme with its homomorphism, so apply the elliptic-curve theorems of Katz-Mazur.

Conrad's route (Thms 2.3.2, 2.3.5, 2.3.7) instead uses artinian reductions, [KM 8.10.7] and universal deformations; Cesnavicius notes that Conrad's proof of Thm 2.4.5 invokes DR III 1.2(iii), which needs the component number prime to the residue characteristic, and supplies Prop. 4.2.11(b) instead.
Prop. 4.2.15: fppf-locally embed E^sm in a decontraction E' and compare functors of E'[N] with those of an elliptic curve E''; ampleness cuts out quasi-compact open subfunctors (EGA IV_3 9.6.4).
acceptance: mu_{p^r}^x = Spec Z[T]/(Phi_{p^r}(T)) and the p-th power map sends it to mu_{p^{r-1}}^x (used in Conrad Thms 2.3.2, 2.3.5).
Rank check (Prop. 4.2.12(b)): Drinfeld (Z/nZ)^2-structures extending a given Z/nZ-structure form a finite locally free scheme of rank n.phi(n).

nodes.title: Full level: X(n) is finite locally free over Ell_n, Cohen-Macaulay, Deligne-Mumford, regular, and equals X_Gamma(n)
nodes.statement: Let X(n) be the Z-stack of pairs (E -> S, alpha) with E a generalized elliptic curve whose degenerate geometric fibres are n-gons and alpha a Drinfeld (Z/nZ)^2-structure on E^sm[n] (automatically ample; over Z[1/n] an isomorphism (Z/nZ)^2 = E[n] on the elliptic locus). (Cesnavicius Prop. 4.3.2) The forgetful f : X(n) -> Ell_n is representable, finite, locally free of degree #GL_2(Z/nZ) and etale over Z[1/n]; hence X(n) is a Cohen-Macaulay reduced algebraic Z-stack, proper and flat of relative dimension 1, smooth over Z[1/n]; X(n)^infinity = f^{-1}(Ell_n^infinity) is a reduced relative effective Cartier divisor meeting every irreducible component of every geometric fibre and smooth over Z[1/n]. (Prop. 4.3.4) The contraction X(nm) -> X(n) is representable, finite, locally free of rank #GL_2(Z/nmZ)/#GL_2(Z/nZ); each X(n) is Deligne-Mumford. (Thm 4.3.5) X(n) is regular and is identified with X_Gamma(n). (Prop. 4.3.6, with n = 1 added) For n >= 2, X(n) is a (necessarily projective) Z-scheme unless n = p^s or n = 2p^s (p prime, s >= 1); X(1) = Ell_1 is not a scheme, since -1 is an automorphism of every object (the printed statement omits n = 1). Conrad reaches the same objects (M_Gamma(N)) with Def. 2.4.2 and Thms 3.1.4, 3.2.7, 3.3.1, 4.1.1(2).
hypotheses: n >= 1; base Spec Z

Regularity imports [KM 5.1.1] (Y(n) regular) and DR V Cor. 4.13 (M^h_n, the complement in the DR stack M_n of the points lying over supersingular points of M_1 in characteristics dividing n, is smooth over Z[zeta_n]; read on DR p. 262), cited by Cesnavicius as '[DR73, 4.13]'

Prop. 4.3.2(b) (boundary meets every irreducible component of every geometric fibre) uses Prop. 3.3.2 (coarse space of Ell_n is P^1_Z with arbitrary base change, so Ell_n has geometrically irreducible Z-fibres), whose n = 1 case over Z is DR VI 1.1, 1.3
proofSteps: Prop. 4.3.2(a) from Prop. 4.2.12(a) (Drinfeld (Z/nZ)^2-structures on E^sm[n] finite locally free of rank #GL_2(Z/nZ)) and Thm 3.1.6(a); CM via EGA IV_2 6.4.2; reducedness via (R_0)+(S_1).

Prop. 4.3.2(b): f does not change E, so X(n)^infinity = X(n) x_{Ell_n} Ell_n^infinity; apply Thm 3.1.6(c)-(d) and Prop. 3.3.2 (geometrically irreducible fibres of Ell_n, placed at R13.4a in this packet; see gap); the only input from the theory over C is that the coarse space of (Ell_1)_C is P^1_C (via DR VI 1.1).
Prop. 4.3.4: representability by Lemma 3.2.2(b) and Lemma 2.1.6; finiteness by Lemma 3.2.3; flatness by factoring c = a o b through Ell_nm x_{Ell_n} X(n) (Thm 3.2.4(a), Prop. 4.2.12(a)).

Thm 4.3.5: Y(n) regular [KM 5.1.1] plus CM gives (R_1)+(S_2), so X(n) is normal; finite over X(1) and agreeing with Y_Gamma(n)[1/n], it is the normalization X_Gamma(n); full regularity by DR V 4.13 away from supersingular points in characteristics dividing n.

Prop. 4.3.6: for n = n_1 n_2 with coprime n_i >= 3, geometric points have no automorphisms ([KM 2.7.2(1)], Lemma 2.1.6) and Lemma 4.1.3 applies; for n = p^s, 2p^s, -1 fixes Drinfeld structures on supersingular curves over F_p-bar; for n = 1, -1 is an automorphism of every object of X(1) = Ell_1.
acceptance: X(1) = Ell_1 and f is the identity for n = 1.
X(15) is not X(3) x_{X(1)} X(5), although Y(15) = Y(3) x_{Y(1)} Y(5): ramification at cusps (Cesnavicius Example 4.5.3).
X(4) (n = 2^2) and X(6) (n = 2.3) are not schemes over Z, whereas X(12) = X(3.4) is a projective Z-scheme (Prop. 4.3.6).

nodes.title: The Weil-pairing morphism M_Gamma(N) -> Spec Z[zeta_N] extends uniquely over Z
nodes.statement: There is a unique morphism M_Gamma(N) -> Spec Z[zeta_N] extending the morphism M^0_Gamma(N)/Z[1/N] -> Spec Z[1/N, zeta_N] defined by the scheme-theoretic Weil pairing of the Drinfeld basis; it is proper, flat and CM (Conrad Thm 4.1.1(3)). The formal chart M_Gamma(N) x_{M_1} Spec Z[[q]] = disjoint union of Spec Z[zeta_N][[q^{1/N}]] is compatible with the Z[zeta_N]-structures on both sides (Conrad Lemma 4.2.4, via the Weil pairing on the Tate curve over Z((q)) and [KM 10.8.2]).
hypotheses: M_Gamma(N) normal, Z-flat, with M^infinity a relative effective Cartier divisor (previous nodes)
proofSteps: Extending zeta_N amounts to extending a root of Phi_N from the complement of the boundary Cartier divisor; normality of the Z-flat stack gives the unique extension.
Properness and flatness follow from Thm 3.3.1; source and target CM, so the flat map is CM.
Compatibility of (4.2.1) with Z[zeta_N] checked after inverting q, where it is [KM 10.8.2] defined via the Weil pairing of the Tate curve.
acceptance: The determinant of the ordered Drinfeld basis matches e_N(P,Q) = zeta_N: the orientation convention (a.d - b.c in DR VII 1.16) must be fixed consistently with the affine #81 object.
For N = 1, 2 the map is Spec Z -> Spec Z (Z[zeta_2] = Z).

Conrad does not define a 'fixed-pairing' stack; if a consumer needs one, define it as the base change of M_Gamma(N) along Spec R -> Spec Z[zeta_N] for a chosen primitive N-th root of unity in R; its geometric connectedness is Conrad Thm 4.2.1(1) (R13.4b), not part of this node.

nodes.title: Gamma_1(n): the stack of ample Drinfeld Z/nZ-structures is proper, regular, Deligne-Mumford and equals X_Gamma1(n)
nodes.statement: Let X_1(n) be the Z-stack of pairs (E -> S, alpha) with alpha an ample Drinfeld Z/nZ-structure on a generalized elliptic curve E, and X_1(n)_(m) the open substack where degenerate fibres are m-gons (m | n). (Cesnavicius Prop. 4.4.2) f_(m) : X_1(n)_(m) -> Ell_m is representable by schemes, quasi-finite, separated, flat, finitely presented and etale over Z[1/n]; X_1(n) is algebraic with quasi-compact separated diagonal, flat of relative dimension 1, smooth over Z[1/n]; X_1(n)^infinity is a reduced relative effective Cartier divisor smooth over Z[1/n]. (Thm 4.4.4) h : X(n) -> X_1(n), (E, alpha) -> (c(E), alpha restricted to Z/nZ x 0), is representable, finite, locally free of rank n.phi(n); X_1(n) is proper over Z and regular and its boundary meets every irreducible component of every geometric fibre; g : X_1(n) -> X(1) is representable, finite, locally free of rank #GL_2(Z/nZ)/(n.phi(n)); X_1(n) is Deligne-Mumford and X_1(n) = X_Gamma1(n), both being the normalization of X(1) in Y_1(n)[1/n] = Y_Gamma1(n)[1/n]. Conrad's M_Gamma_1(N) (Def. 2.4.1) is the same stack, with regularity at the cusps proved by explicit computation (R13.3).
hypotheses: n >= 1; base Spec Z; Gamma_1(n) = matrices with a = 1 mod n, c = 0 mod n in GL_2(Z-hat)
proofSteps: Prop. 4.4.2 from Prop. 4.2.15(a) and 4.2.7(a); the open substacks X_1(n)_(m) cover.

Thm 4.4.4(a): f_(m) o h_(m) equals X(n)_(m) -> Ell_n -> Ell_m (identification (3.2.1.2)); h_(m) factors as h' : X(n)_(m) -> X_1(n)_(m) x_{Ell_m} Ell_n, finite locally free of rank n.phi(n) by Prop. 4.2.12(b), followed by the proper flat surjective base change of c (Thm 3.2.4(a)); h is quasi-finite, hence finite locally free (Lemma 3.2.3); separatedness of X_1(n) from that of X(n) and surjectivity of h; regularity descends from X(n) along the flat surjection h (EGA IV_2 6.5.3(i)).
(b): g proper, representable (Lemma 3.2.2(b), Lemma 2.1.6), quasi-finite, hence finite; rank from g o h.
(c): an S-point of the quotient of Isom(E[n], (Z/nZ)^2) by the stabilizer of (1,0) amounts to an isomorphism from Z/nZ onto a subgroup of E (Remark 4.2.3).
acceptance: Rank check at n = p prime: h has rank p(p-1) and g has rank (p^2 - 1)(p^2 - p)/(p(p-1)) = p^2 - 1.
X_1(4) over F_2: coarse space base change fails (Cesnavicius Remark 6.6), although the stack is regular.

nodes.title: Cesnavicius's axiomatic criterion: a candidate stack with a proper flat surjection from X(n) and a representable map to X(1) is regular and equals X_H
nodes.statement: Let H c GL_2(Z-hat) be open, n >= 1 with Gamma(n) c H, and X'_H a Z-stack. (a) If X'_H is covered by open substacks (X'_H)_(m), m | n, each admitting a morphism (X'_H)_(m) -> Ell_d(m) (some d(m) >= 1) that is representable by algebraic spaces, separated and of finite type, then X'_H is algebraic with quasi-compact separated diagonal and of finite type over Z. (b) If X'_H is algebraic, has quasi-compact separated diagonal, is of finite type over Z, and (1) there is a proper flat surjective Z-morphism h : X(n) -> X'_H, then X'_H is regular, X'_H -> Spec Z is a proper flat surjection, and (X'_H)_Z[1/n] is Z[1/n]-smooth. (c) If X'_H is algebraic, Z-proper and satisfies (1) together with (2) a Z-morphism g : X'_H -> X(1), representable by algebraic spaces, identified over Z[1/n] with Y_H[1/n] -> Y(1)_Z[1/n], and (3) g o h equal to the contraction X(n) -> X(1) of 4.3.3, then X'_H is Deligne-Mumford and g induces X_H = X'_H, both being the normalization of X(1) in Y_H[1/n] (Cesnavicius Thm 4.5.1). Flatness of h is the most stringent requirement, supplied by Katz-Mazur through congruences (Remark 4.5.2).
hypotheses: As stated in (a)-(c); X(n) regular (previous full-level node)
proofSteps: (a): algebraicity of each open from Ell_d(m) (LMB 4.5(ii)); the diagonal factors through the quasi-compact open union of the (X'_H)_(m) x (X'_H)_(m).
(b): properness of the diagonal from (h x h) o Delta_X(n) and surjectivity of h; flatness, regularity and smoothness descend along the flat surjection h from X(n).
(c): g representable gives Deligne-Mumford; g proper and quasi-finite hence finite; X'_H normal by (b), so g identifies it with the normalization.
acceptance: Example 4.5.3: H = Gamma(d) intersect Gamma_1(l) with coprime d, l gives a regular X_H with the 'obvious' description; regularity at cusps is not automatic from X_Gamma(d), X_Gamma1(l).

nodes.title: Mixed level X~_1(n;n'), X_1(n;n'), X_0(n;n'): algebraic, regular, proper and flat; large Deligne-Mumford open substacks; identification with X_H under ord_p conditions
nodes.statement: For n, n' >= 1, d = gcd(n,n'), X_1(n;n') parametrizes (E, alpha, H) with alpha a Drinfeld Z/nZ-structure on some G c E^sm and H c E^sm cyclic of order n' such that [G_d + H_d] = E^sm[d] and [G + H] is ample (4.6.1.1); X~_1 replaces H by a Drinfeld Z/n'Z-structure and X_0(n;n') replaces alpha by a cyclic G of order n (4.6.2). (Thm 4.6.4) Each of these stacks is algebraic, regular, proper, flat and of relative dimension 1 over Z, smooth over Z[1/nn'], with finite diagonal; the contraction X(nn') -> X is representable by schemes, finite locally free of constant positive rank; X^infinity is a reduced relative effective Cartier divisor meeting every component of every geometric fibre, smooth over Z[1/nn']. (Prop. 4.6.5) X~_1(n;n') is Deligne-Mumford and X~_1(n;n') -> X(1) is representable; X_1(n;n') minus its boundary in characteristics p with ord_p(n') >= ord_p(n) + 2 is Deligne-Mumford, and X_1(n;n') -> X(1) is representable if ord_p(n') <= ord_p(n) + 1 for all p; X_0(n;n') minus its boundary in characteristics p with |ord_p(n) - ord_p(n')| >= 2 is Deligne-Mumford, and X_0(n;n') -> X(1) is representable if |ord_p(n) - ord_p(n')| <= 1 for all p. (Thm 4.6.6) Accordingly X~_1(n;n') = X_{Gamma~_1(n;n')} always, X_1(n;n') = X_{Gamma_1(n;n')} if ord_p(n') <= ord_p(n) + 1 for every p, and X_0(n;n') = X_{Gamma_0(n;n')} if |ord_p(n') - ord_p(n)| <= 1 for every p. X_1(n;n') agrees with Conrad's M_Gamma_1(n;n') where the latter is defined (ord_p(n') <= ord_p(n) for p | gcd); outside ord_p(n') <= 1 for p not dividing n Conrad's stack has non-representable contraction to X(1) even over C.
hypotheses: n, n' >= 1 arbitrary for Thm 4.6.4
The ord_p inequalities exactly as stated for Prop. 4.6.5 and Thm 4.6.6 (checked on the image of arXiv p. 48)
proofSteps: Thm 4.6.4(a): the forgetful maps X_(m) -> Ell_m are representable, separated, finite type (Prop. 4.2.15(a) and finiteness of X~_1 -> X_1 -> X_0 (4.6.2.1), ranks phi(n'), phi(n)), so Thm 4.5.1(a) gives algebraicity; X(nn') -> X~_1(n;n') is proper flat surjective because X(nn')_(m) -> X~_1(n;n')_(m) x_{Ell_m} Ell_nn' is finite locally free (Prop. 4.2.12(a),(d)) and Thm 3.2.4(a); Thm 4.5.1(b) gives the rest.

Prop. 4.6.5: test unramified automorphism functors at geometric points using Aut(standard m-gon) = mu_m x Z/2Z; reduce to p-power n, n', m and show mu_p cannot fix the data under the stated inequalities (ampleness, standard cyclic subgroups H_p = mu_p, [G_p + H_p] = E^sm[p]).
Thm 4.6.6: with representability, apply Thm 4.6.4 and Thm 4.5.1(c), comparing Y-stacks over Z[1/nn'] with the double-coset descriptions of the three groups.
acceptance: n' = 1: X_0(n;1) = X_0(n)^naive (next node).
n = N, n' = p prime: X_1(N;p) = X_Gamma1(N;p), the source of the Hecke correspondence (R14.1).
