nodes.title: The naive Gamma_0(n) stack (ample cyclic subgroups) is regular and proper but differs from X_Gamma0(n) when p^2 | n, even over C
nodes.statement: X_0(n)^naive, the Z-stack of generalized elliptic curves with an ample cyclic subgroup G c E^sm of order n, equals X_0(n;1); it is algebraic, proper and flat over Z and regular with finite diagonal, X(n) -> X_0(n)^naive is finite locally free of rank n.phi(n)^2, and for squarefree n the contraction X_0(n)^naive -> X(1) is the structure map of X_Gamma0(n) (Cesnavicius 5.1). If p^2 | n, the contraction c : X_0(n)^naive -> X(1) is not representable, even over C: for E the standard p-gon over C and zeta a primitive p^2-th root of unity, the mu_p of automorphisms fixing G_m x {0} stabilizes the cyclic subgroup generated by (zeta, 1) of order p^2 and contracts to the identity; over F_p the same example shows X_0(p^2)^naive is not Deligne-Mumford (Cesnavicius 1.2, also [Edi90 1.1.1.1], [Con07]). Since X_0(p^2) -> X(1) is representable by construction, X_0(n)^naive and X_Gamma0(n) are genuinely different for non-squarefree n.
hypotheses: n >= 1; the failure requires p^2 | n for some prime p
proofSteps: Properties of X_0(n;1) from Thm 4.6.4; squarefree identification from Thm 4.6.6(c) since |ord_p(n) - ord_p(1)| <= 1.

Non-representability: exhibit the mu_p of automorphisms of the standard p-gon acting by zeta^i on component i; it fixes G_m x {0} pointwise and stabilizes the subgroup generated by (zeta_{p^2},1), yet contracts to the identity of the 1-gon.
acceptance: n = 4 over C: the standard 2-gon with the cyclic subgroup of order 4 generated by (i,1) has a non-trivial automorphism (x -> -x on component 1) fixing the level structure and trivial on the contraction.
Coarse spaces of X_0(n)^naive and the refined X_0(n) agree (R13.4a), so the difference is invisible on coarse moduli.

nodes.title: Refined Gamma_0(n)-structures (Deligne's suggestion): subdivision of the degeneracy locus and coherent ample cyclic subgroups of universal decontractions
nodes.statement: Fix n >= 1 and for m | n put d(m) = m / gcd(m, n/m) (checked on the image of arXiv p. 50). For a generalized elliptic curve pi : E -> S, a Gamma_0(n)-structure is (G, {S_pi,(m)}, {G_(m)}) with: (1) a cyclic subgroup G c E_{S - S^infinity} of order n; (2) opens S_pi,(m) c S (m | n) covering S, pairwise intersecting in S - S^infinity, with degenerate geometric fibres of E over S_pi,(m) being d(m)-gons; (3) for each m | n an ample cyclic subgroup G_(m) of order n of the universal decontraction E_pi,(m) over the algebraic stack S_pi,(m) x_{Ell_d(m)} Ell_m (which parametrizes (E' -> S', iota' : E_S' = c_{E'^sm[d(m)]}(E'))), agreeing with G on the elliptic locus and coherent (5.5: fpqc-locally, pullbacks along any two objects have generators meeting the same components and with equal images iota^{-1}((n/m) g)). The stack X_0(n) (5.10) has objects (E, Gamma_0(n)-structure) as in 5.9, and morphisms only between tuples with the same opens S_pi,(m), consisting of an isomorphism of E carrying G to G together with isomorphisms of the decontraction data carrying G_(m) to G_(m); Y_0(n) = Y_0(n)^naive; for squarefree n, d(m) = m and X_0(n) = X_0(n)^naive (Remark 5.9.3); coherence is automatic when n is invertible (Lemma 5.6). There is a contraction X_0(n)^naive -> X_0(n) gluing contractions c_{E^sm[d(m)]} and using Lemma 5.7 to define G_(m) (5.11). Lemma 5.7 (existence and uniqueness of the transported cyclic subgroup G' on a curve E' with d-gon fibres and iota between contractions, with properties (i)-(iv)) is the key technical input.
hypotheses: n >= 1 fixed; m ranges over positive divisors of n
Coherence (3.2) needed to handle characteristics dividing n
proofSteps: 5.2: for the standard m-gon with ample cyclic G, G intersect (E^sm)^0 = mu_{n/m}, mu_m c Aut(E) acts trivially on the contraction to the zero section, and the stabilizer of G in it is mu_{gcd(m,n/m)}, which acts trivially on exactly d(m) components; so only the contraction to a d(m)-gon plus the standard cyclic subgroup of order (n/m).d(m) is remembered, together with compatible G on all m-gon decontractions.
Lemma 5.4: canonical identification of component groups of decontractions compatible with iota (Lemma 2.1.6).

Lemma 5.7 steps: (iv) from the rest; (iii) via Prop. 3.2.7(a) extensions 0 -> B_n -> A_{n,m} -> C_m -> 0 over a complete noetherian base (using Cor. 3.2.5 to compare adic topologies); reduction to prime-power n; case s = 0; uniqueness via standard cyclic subgroups and Prop. 4.2.9(f); existence via choosing g' with (m/d(m)) g' = iota((m/d(m)) g), adjusting its C_m-image, Prop. 4.2.5(d), and comparison over S - S^infinity through Prop. 3.1.8(b) on a DVR.
5.10: pairs (i_(m), i_E(m)) compatible with i_E exist uniquely up to unique isomorphism, so X_0(n)(S) is a groupoid and X_0(n) is an fppf Z-stack.
acceptance: n = p^2 over Z[1/p]: Deligne's description in 1.3 (subdivision S_(1), S_(p), S_(p^2); G_(p) living on the universal decontraction E_(p), a stack) is recovered.

d(m) for n = 12: d(1) = 1, d(2) = 2/gcd(2,6) = 1, d(3) = 3/gcd(3,4) = 3, d(4) = 4/gcd(4,3) = 4, d(6) = 6/gcd(6,2) = 3, d(12) = 12; so the opens S_(1) and S_(2) both carry 1-gon degenerate fibres and S_(3), S_(6) both carry 3-gons, which is why m is part of the data (5.2).

nodes.title: Theorem: the refined X_0(n) is a regular Deligne-Mumford stack equal to X_Gamma0(n) for every n, with reduced boundary Cartier divisor
nodes.statement: (Cesnavicius Lemma 5.12) For m | n, X_0(n)^naive_(m) = X_0(n)_(m) x_{Ell_d(m)} Ell_m (Cartesian square), and X_0(n)_(m) -> Ell_d(m) is representable by schemes, finitely presented, separated, quasi-finite, flat, and etale over Z[1/n]. (Thm 5.13) X_0(n) is Deligne-Mumford and regular; the map X_0(n) -> X(1) forgetting the structure and contracting with respect to the identity section identifies X_0(n) = X_Gamma0(n), both being the normalization of X(1) in Y_0(n)[1/n] = Y_Gamma0(n)[1/n]; X_0(n)^infinity is a reduced relative effective Cartier divisor over Z meeting every irreducible component of every geometric fibre and smooth over Z[1/n]. This extends the regularity theorem of Katz-Mazur for Y_0(n) to the cusps; X_0(n)Z[1/n] was already Z[1/n]-smooth by DR IV 6.7.
hypotheses: n >= 1 arbitrary (no squarefree hypothesis)
Imports: regularity of X(n) (full-level node) and of Y_0(n) [KM 5.1.1]
proofSteps: Lemma 5.12(a): the coherence condition and uniqueness in Lemma 5.7 make X_0(n)_(m) x Ell_m -> X_0(n)^naive_(m) inverse to the map induced by the contraction of 5.11.

Lemma 5.12(b): X_0(n)^naive_(m) -> Ell_m has the properties by Prop. 4.2.15(a); they are fppf local on the target and Ell_m -> Ell_d(m) is flat surjective finitely presented (Thm 3.2.4(a)), so they descend via (a).

Thm 5.13(a): Thm 4.5.1(a) with the cover by X_0(n)_(m); (b) with h = X(n) -> X_0(n)^naive -> X_0(n), proper flat surjective by 5.1, Lemma 5.12(a) and Thm 3.2.4(a); (c) with Y_0(n) = Y_0(n)^naive and the image of Gamma_0(n) the stabilizer of Z/nZ x 0.

Representability of X_0(n) -> X(1) (Lemma 3.2.2(b)): if i in mu_p(A) c Aut(E) (E the standard d-gon, A artinian over k-bar) fixed alpha_A, lift through the decontraction to i~ in mu_m(A) stabilizing G~, hence i~ in mu_{gcd(m,n/m)}(A), which acts trivially on c_{E~^sm[d]}(E~), forcing i = id.
Thm 5.13(b): surjectivity of X(n) -> X_0(n), Prop. 4.3.2(b), and on each X_0(n)_(m) the boundary is the preimage of Ell_d(m)^infinity (Thm 3.1.6(c)-(d), Lemma 5.12(b)).
acceptance: For squarefree n, X_0(n) = X_0(n)^naive and Thm 5.13 reduces to Thm 4.6.6(c).
At n = p^2 the cusps of X_0(p^2) in characteristic p are Deligne-Mumford points, unlike those of X_0(p^2)^naive.

nodes.title: Schematic loci: the open subscheme of automorphism-free points, fine moduli schemes for level >= 5 (resp. >= 3) and ampleness of the boundary
nodes.statement: (Conrad Thm 4.2.1(2)) Let Gamma = Gamma_1(N;n) with n squarefree (resp. Gamma(N)) over S = Spec Z (resp. Spec Z[zeta_N]). There is an open subscheme M^sch of M_Gamma whose geometric points are exactly those with trivial automorphism group; if d | N and d >= 5 (resp. d >= 3), M_Gamma over S[1/d] lies in M^sch and M^infinity over S[1/d] is relatively ample. Remark 4.2.2 concludes that 'for large N' the Katz-Mazur proper flat schemes X_1(N)/Z and X(N)^can/Z[zeta_N] coincide with M_Gamma_1(N) and M_Gamma(N)/Z[zeta_N] and are fine moduli schemes for Drinfeld structures on generalized elliptic curves. 'Large' is not made precise. Thm 4.2.1(2) gives a scheme over all of S when N has two coprime divisors d, d' >= 5 (resp. >= 3), since S[1/d] and S[1/d'] then cover S (reviewer's deduction; compare Cesnavicius Prop. 4.3.6 for full level). A single divisor d >= 5 gives a fine moduli scheme only over S[1/d]: M_Gamma_1(5) is not a scheme in characteristic 5, because M^infinity_{Gamma_1(5),1} is not. For Gamma_1(N) and d | N, points of M^infinity_{Gamma_1(N),d} have trivial automorphism functors when d > 2, so these cusps lie in M^sch over Z; M^infinity_{Gamma_1(N),1} is not a scheme in characteristic p > 0 iff N in {p^s, 2p^s} (s >= 0), and M^infinity_{Gamma_1(N),2} is not iff N = 2p^s (s >= 0) (Conrad 4.3, before Def. 4.3.3). Caveat (reviewer finding): the d = 2 criterion appears to omit N = 4p^s with p odd and s >= 1. In characteristic p the ample Gamma_1(N)-structure P = (i,1) on the standard 2-gon (i a primitive 4th root of unity) is fixed by inversion followed by -1 in mu_2. So M^infinity_{Gamma_1(4p^s),2} is not a scheme in characteristic p (e.g. N = 12, p = 3); see the gap on Conrad Def. 4.3.3.
hypotheses: n squarefree for Gamma_1(N;n)
d | N with d >= 5 for Gamma_1, d >= 3 for Gamma(N), and d inverted on the base for the fine-moduli statement
proofSteps: Existence of M^sch as a separated open algebraic subspace from Thm 2.2.5 (automorphism functors of geometric points are etale); it is a scheme since M_1 maps quasi-finitely to the j-line P^1_Z by the sections Delta and c_4^3 of omega^12.
Automorphism-freeness for M >= 5 (resp. >= 3) with level prime to the characteristic, reduced from Gamma_1(M;n) to Gamma_1(M) by Lemma 4.2.3.

Ampleness of the boundary: every component of a geometric fibre maps onto (M_1)_s; reduce via finite flat contractions to Lemma 4.2.4 (the boundary of M_Gamma(N) lies in the smooth locus over Z[zeta_N]) using the Tate chart (4.2.1).
acceptance: Gamma_1(5) over Z[1/5] is a fine moduli scheme. Gamma_1(4) is not, even over Z[1/2]: (N,d) = (4,2) is a nowhere-schematic case of Conrad Def. 4.3.3; on the standard 2-gon with P = (i,1), i a primitive 4th root of unity, the automorphism (inversion followed by zeta = -1 in mu_2) fixes P (worker check of Conrad Lemma 3.1.8, case d = 2, x^2 in mu_2).

Cesnavicius Prop. 4.3.6 (p. 39): X(n) is a projective Z-scheme unless n = p^s or 2p^s with s >= 1, and is not a scheme in those cases. As printed the proposition also covers n = 1, where X(1) = Ell_1 is not a scheme: -1 is an automorphism of every object, and the proof's factorization n = n_1 n_2 with coprime n_1, n_2 >= 3 is unavailable. n = 2 = 2^1 is already excluded as p^s. The list is correct for n >= 2.

nodes.title: Tate_n is the unique generalized elliptic curve over Z[[q^{1/n}]] with n-gon fibres at q^{1/n} = 0 extending Tate_1 over Z((q^{1/n}))
nodes.statement: For all n >= 1, Tate_n -> Spec Z[[q^{1/n}]] is, up to unique isomorphism, the unique generalized elliptic curve restricting to Tate_1 tensor_{Z[[q]]} Z((q^{1/n})) over Spec Z((q^{1/n})) and having n-gon geometric fibres over q^{1/n} = 0; the isomorphism over Z((q^{1/n})) is uniquely characterized by respecting the identifications of the formal groups at the origin of Tate_n and Tate_1 with G_m-hat (Conrad Thm 2.5.2). More precisely the contraction of Tate_n away from its fibral identity components is naturally Tate_1(q) over Z[[q^{1/n}]] compatibly with G_m-hat.
hypotheses: n >= 1; base Z[[q^{1/n}]]; the isomorphism respects (2.5.3)
proofSteps: Uniqueness: Tate_n has n-gon fibres over the Cartier divisor q^{1/n} = 0, so by Conrad Cor. 3.2.5 it is determined by its restriction over q^{1/n} != 0 (Cor. 3.2.5 does not depend on Section 2.5).

Existence of the identification is a special case of DR VII 1.14: contracting Tate_{kn}(q^{1/n}) to Tate_k(q) modulo (q^{1/n})^m for fixed k > 1 and all m, then passing to quotients by the free actions of kZ/knZ and Z/kZ; formal GAGA and compatibility of contraction with base change give the statement over Z[[q^{1/n}]].
Compatibility with (2.5.3) may be checked modulo q^{1/n}, since all maximal ideals of Z have positive residue characteristic.
acceptance: For n = 1 the statement is tautological.
Used to define Tate^reg in the cusp charts (Thm 4.3.6) and in the extension of pi_2 (R14.1).

nodes.title: Formal chart of M_Gamma(N) along the cusps: M_Gamma(N) x_{M_1} Spec Z[[q]] is a disjoint union of Spec Z[zeta_N][[q^{1/N}]], compatibly with the Weil pairing; the boundary lies in the smooth locus over Z[zeta_N]
nodes.statement: For N >= 1 there is a finite disjoint union decomposition M_Gamma(N) x_{M_1} Spec Z[[q]] = disjoint union of copies of Spec(Z[zeta_N][[q^{1/N}]]) as Z[[q]]-schemes (the normalization of Z[[q]] in the scheme of Gamma(N)-structures on Tate_1 over Z((q)), computed in [KM 10.8.2]); it is compatible with the Z[zeta_N]-structures (Weil pairing morphism on the left). Consequently M^infinity_Gamma(N) lies in the smooth locus of M_Gamma(N) -> Spec Z[zeta_N], universal deformation rings at k-points of M^infinity_Gamma(N) (k = Q-bar or F_p-bar) are formally smooth over W[zeta_N], and M_Gamma(N) is regular along its cusps (Conrad Thm 4.1.1 proof, Lemma 4.2.4).
hypotheses: N >= 1 arbitrary (no invertibility of N)
Spec W[[q]] -> M_1 is the algebraized universal deformation of the 1-gon (R13.1)
proofSteps: Regularity reduction: at a k-point of M^infinity_Gamma, a local factor of M_Gamma x_{M_1} Spec W[[q]] is a finite etale cover of the complete local ring of M_Gamma at that point (Lemma 3.3.5), so it suffices to prove regularity of M_Gamma x_{M_1} Spec W[[q]]; Z[[q]] -> W[[q]] is a regular morphism since Z[[q]] is excellent and W[[q]] is the completion of a strict henselization of Z[[q]] at (p, q) (Lemma 4.1.6, Thm 2.2.8(2)); so it suffices to treat M_Gamma x_{M_1} Spec Z[[q]].
That scheme is normal (regular in characteristics prime to N) by excellence (Lemma 4.1.7), hence it is the normalization of Z[[q]] in the scheme of Gamma(N)-structures on Tate_1 over Z((q)).
[KM 10.8.2] computes the latter as a finite disjoint union of Spec Z[zeta_N]((q^{1/N})), whose normalization is the regular disjoint union of Spec Z[zeta_N][[q^{1/N}]].

Lemma 4.2.4: Z[zeta_N]-compatibility is checked after inverting q (by flatness), where (4.2.1) is the Katz-Mazur isomorphism defined by the Weil pairing on the Tate curve; formal smoothness follows because Spec W[[q]] -> M_1 is a uniquely algebraized universal deformation (Lemma 3.3.5) and completion commutes with finite algebras.
acceptance: Cusp width check: each component of the formal chart has parameter q^{1/N}, i.e. every cusp of the full level curve has width N relative to q.

Reviewer check (not a source claim): over F_p the boundary fibre of each chart is Spec(Z[zeta_N] tensor F_p) = Spec F_p[x]/(Phi_N(x)), which is non-reduced exactly when p | N and p^{ord_p(N)} != 2 (for N = 2m with m odd and p = 2 it is reduced, since Z[zeta_{2m}] = Z[zeta_m]); so the flat cusp divisor and its reduced locus in characteristic p must be kept distinct.

nodes.title: Regularity of M_Gamma1(N) along the cusps: normalization of Z[[q]] in the Gamma_1(N)-structures on Tate_1 and the invariant-ring computation, including N = 2^r
nodes.statement: By [KM 7.4.3, 10.5.1(2)] the scheme of Gamma_1(N)-structures on Tate_1 over Z((q)) is the disjoint union over representatives Lambda_i of HomSurj((Z/NZ)^2, Z/NZ)/G of Spec Z[zeta_N]((q^{1/N}))^{G intersect Fix(Lambda_i)}, with G the group of matrices (1 *; 0 *) in GL_2(Z/NZ) and the GL_2(Z/NZ)-action defined on Z[zeta_N][q^{1/N}] as in [KM 10.5]. Its normalization over Z[[q]] is the disjoint union of Spec Z[zeta_N][[q^{1/N}]]^{G intersect Fix(Lambda_i)}, and these rings are regular; hence M_Gamma1(N) is regular (Conrad Thm 4.1.1(2)). Regularity at residue characteristic p | N reduces to the invariant rings Z_(p)[zeta_N][q^{1/N}]^{G intersect Fix(Lambda_i)}; after reducing N to its p-part by the method of proof of [KM 10.10.3], [KM 10.10.4] settles p != 2, N = 2 and N = 2^r with det(G intersect Fix(Lambda_i)) = 1 mod 4; the remaining cases N = 2^r, r >= 2, det not = 1 mod 4 are computed directly, with representatives {(a,0) : a odd} union {(a,1) : a even}: for odd a, G intersect Fix(a,0) = {(1 0; 0 *)} and the invariant ring is Z_(2)[q^{1/N}]; for even a = 2a' (a' odd), after upper-triangularization ([KM 10.3.4]) the group is {(1-ax, x; 0, 1)}, its even-x subgroup has invariant ring Z_(2)[i][zeta (q^{1/2^r})^2] with i = zeta_{2^r}^{2^{r-2}} and zeta = zeta_{2^r}^{1/a'}, and the full invariant ring is Z_(2)[zeta (q^{1/2^r})^2], which is regular. For Gamma_1(N;n) with p | gcd(N,n), regularity reduces to Gamma_1(M) cases: in the non-ample case the deformation rings are W[[t]] tensor_Z Z[zeta_{p^r}], already regular; in the ample case B = A[zeta_{p^e}] with A a Gamma_1(M) deformation ring, and passage to (Z/p^eZ)^x-invariants shows the complete local rings of M_Gamma1(N;n) are formally smooth over A.
hypotheses: N >= 1; the Gamma_1(N;n) reduction uses the Deligne-Mumford cover M_{Gamma~_1(N;n)}
proofSteps: Flat base change Z[q] -> Z[[q]] commutes with finite-group invariants, and A -> A-hat is regular for excellent A (EGA IV_2 7.8.3(v)), so it suffices to check regularity of Z_(p)[zeta_N][q^{1/N}]^{G intersect Fix(Lambda_i)} for p | N.

Case analysis for p = 2 as in Conrad p. 35: representatives {(a,0) : a odd} union {(a,1) : a even}; for odd a, [KM 10.3.2] shows G intersect Fix(a,0) acts through the determinant on roots of unity and fixes q^{1/N}; for even a, the upper-triangularized group (4.1.7) = {(1-ax, x; 0, 1)} acts through (r s; 0 1) : (zeta_N, q^{1/N}) -> (zeta_N^r, zeta_N^s q^{1/N}); its even-x subgroup has invariants Z_(2)[i][zeta (q^{1/2^r})^2]; the element (1-a, 1; 0, 1) sends i to i^{1-2a'} = -i and zeta (q^{1/2^r})^2 to zeta^{1-a}(zeta_{2^r} q^{1/2^r})^2 = zeta (q^{1/2^r})^2, so the invariant ring is Z_(2)[zeta (q^{1/2^r})^2].

Gamma_1(N;n): completed local rings O^_{U',u'} = O^_{U,u} tensor Z[zeta_{p^e}] equivariantly for (Z/p^eZ)^x, so O^_{U,u} is formally smooth over the complete local ring A of a Gamma_1(M) stack, hence regular if A is (Conrad pp. 32-33).
acceptance: N = 4: the G-orbits of surjective functionals have representatives (1,0), (3,0), (0,1), (2,1), indexing the components of M_Gamma1(4) x_{M_1} Spec Z[[q]]; (0,1) has det(G intersect Fix) = 1 and is covered by [KM 10.10.4], (1,0) and (3,0) give Z_(2)[q^{1/4}], and (2,1) (a' = 1) is the case needing the explicit computation, with invariant ring Z_(2)[zeta (q^{1/4})^2], zeta a primitive 4th root of unity.
Cesnavicius obtains the same regularity without this computation (Thm 4.4.4(a)); both must agree.

nodes.title: The cusp substacks M^infinity_{Gamma_1(N),d}: reduced, regular, finite flat over Z; Z[zeta_{N/d}]-components for d > 2; totally real rings and degree-2 covers for d <= 2; nowhere- and partially-schematic cases
nodes.statement: For Gamma in {Gamma(N), Gamma_1(N;n)} and d >= 1, M^infinity_{Gamma,d} (degenerate fibres d-gons) is an open and closed substack of M^infinity_Gamma and a reduced relative Cartier divisor in M_Gamma (Conrad Def. 4.3.1, Lemma 4.3.2). For Gamma_1(N) and d | N (Thm 4.3.4): M^infinity_{Gamma_1(N),d} is regular of pure relative dimension 0 over Spec Z, proper, quasi-finite and flat over Z. If d > 2 it is a finite non-empty disjoint union of copies of Spec Z[zeta_{N/d}], indexed by pairs (b, r) with b in (Z/dZ)^x and r a positive divisor of d reducing to a unit in Z/(N/d)Z. If d <= 2: in the schematic cases it is Spec Z[zeta_{N/d}]^+ (ring of integers of the maximal totally real subfield of Q(zeta_{N/d})); in general there is a relatively representable degree-2 finite flat covering Spec Z[zeta_{N/d}] -> M^infinity_{Gamma_1(N),d}, finite etale if d = 1, and finite etale after inverting 2 if d = 2, in the nowhere-schematic cases (N,d) in {(1,1),(2,1),(2,2),(4,2)}; in the partially-schematic cases (N,d) in {(p^s,1)} union {(2p^s,1),(2p^s,2)} (s > 0, excluding the nowhere-schematic ones), with delta_{N,d} = p, it restricts over Z[1/delta] to Spec Z[zeta_{N/d}][1/delta] -> Spec Z[zeta_{N/d}]^+[1/delta]. According to Conrad, M^infinity_{Gamma_1(N),d} is a scheme in the schematic cases, a scheme over Z[1/delta] in the partially-schematic cases, and nowhere a scheme in the nowhere-schematic cases (Def. 4.3.3; statements checked on the image of p. 38). Reviewer caveat (not in the source): Conrad's claim that M^infinity_{Gamma_1(N),2} fails to be a scheme in characteristic p only for N = 2p^s appears to omit N = 4p^s with p odd and s >= 1. In characteristic p the point (C_2, P = (i,1)), i a primitive 4th root of unity, is an ample Gamma_1(N)-structure fixed by inversion composed with -1 in mu_2, so for (N,d) = (4p^s,2) the stack is not a scheme at p and the schematic-case description Spec Z[zeta_{N/2}]^+ can hold only over Z[1/p]; these cases should be treated as partially schematic with delta = p (see gap).
hypotheses: N >= 1, d | N; Gamma = Gamma_1(N) for Thm 4.3.4 (Conrad: other cases 'by similar arguments', excluding for Gamma_1(N;n) the geometric points with p-part of C neither etale nor connected, which occur iff p^2 | n)
proofSteps: Lemma 4.3.2: Z-flatness reduces reducedness to the generic fibre; over an artin local ring with algebraically closed residue field of characteristic 0, B^x is divisible, so fppf-locally standard polygons are standard; the automorphism scheme of the standard d-gon over Q is etale, so the Q-fibre is etale.

Residue fields over Q: every Gamma_1(N)-structure on C_d over Q-bar is defined over Q(zeta_N). For d = 1: (C_1, zeta_N) induces all structures, and embeddings related by complex conjugation give isomorphic ones (Aut(C_1) = <inv>), so the residue field is Q(zeta_N)^+. For d = 2: (C_2, (zeta_N, 1)) induces all structures, (C_2,(zeta_N,1)) and (C_2,(-zeta_N,1)) are isomorphic, and the residue field is Q(zeta_{N/2})^+ (for N/2 odd this equals Q(zeta_N)^+). For d > 2: structures (C_d, (zeta_N^r, b)) with b in (Z/dZ)^x, r | N a unit mod N/d; (C_d,(zeta_N^{ra}, b)) is isomorphic iff a = 1 mod N/d, giving residue field Q(zeta_{N/d}).

Over Z: M^infinity is proper, quasi-finite, flat (relative Cartier divisor); the maps Spec Z[zeta_{N/d}] -> M^infinity for d <= 2 are finite surjections; regularity: Gamma_1(N)-structures on Tate_d over W[zeta_N][[q^{1/d}]] (Lemma 2.3.1) give a finite map to the complete local rings A_d of M_Gamma1(N) at F_p-bar-points, flat by Lemma 4.1.3 (A_d regular since M_Gamma1(N) is regular; finite etale covers finite flat over W[[q]] by Lemma 3.3.5) and faithfully flat by the characteristic-0 surjectivity; the ideal of topological nilpotents of A_d cuts out the non-smooth locus (Lemma 4.3.2) and pulls back to (q^{1/d}) (Thm 2.1.12), so M^infinity has a faithfully flat regular cover Spec W[zeta_N].
Etaleness in nowhere-schematic cases: degree-2 covers are etale away from 2; for d = 1, N <= 2 the map is an fppf Aut(C_1) = Z/2Z-torsor.
acceptance: Distinguish three assertions (README): M^infinity is a reduced relative Cartier divisor flat over Z (Lemma 4.3.2, Thm 4.1.1(1)); for d > 2 its fibre over F_p is a disjoint union of copies of Spec(Z[zeta_{N/d}] tensor F_p), which is non-reduced exactly when p | N/d and p^{ord_p(N/d)} != 2 (reviewer check); its reduced locus is a different subscheme.

Stabilizer checks (reviewer computations, not in the source): on the standard 2-gon, inversion followed by -1 in mu_2 fixes P = (x,1) whenever x^2 = -1; this gives the non-trivial automorphism at the (4,2) cusp in every characteristic != 2 and, in characteristic p odd, at P = (i,1) for N = 4p^s (a case missing from Def. 4.3.3, see gap). In characteristic p with N = 2p^s the only geometric points P = (+-1, 1) are fixed by inversion alone, matching Conrad's partially-schematic list.

nodes.title: Cusp charts for d > 2: Tate^reg(zeta_{N/d}^{-r} q) over Z[zeta_{N/d}][[q^{1/d}]] with Gamma_1(N)-structure q^{b/d} is the (b,r')-component of the formal completion (cusp width d)
nodes.statement: For N >= 1, d | N and r in (Z/(N/d)Z)^x there is a unique generalized elliptic curve Tate^reg(zeta_{N/d}^{-r} q) -> Spec Z[zeta_{N/d}][[q^{1/d}]] with d-gon geometric fibres over q^{1/d} = 0 that is isomorphic to Tate_1(zeta_{N/d}^{-r} q) over q^{1/d} != 0; its locus of non-smoothness is (q^{1/d}), and after the base change zeta_{N/d} -> zeta_N^d it becomes Tate_d(zeta_N^{-r'} q^{1/d}) over Z[zeta_N][[q^{1/d}]] for any lift r'. For b' in (Z/NZ)^x lifting b in (Z/dZ)^x, the Gamma_1(N)-structure 'q^{b/d}' (from the canonical splitting (2.5.2)) on Tate_d(zeta_N^{-r'b'^{-1}} q^{1/d}) descends uniquely to Tate^reg(zeta_{N/d}^{-rb'^{-1}} q). If d > 2 and r is normalized (up to (Z/(N/d)Z)^x) to lift to r' | d with r' > 0, the resulting map Spec Z[zeta_{N/d}][[q^{1/d}]] -> M_Gamma1(N) lands in the schematic locus and identifies Spf Z[zeta_{N/d}][[q^{1/d}]] with the (b,r')-component of the formal completion of M_Gamma1(N) along M^infinity_{Gamma_1(N),d}; this computes its algebraization (Conrad Thm 4.3.6). The base change Tate_1(zeta_{N/d}^{-r} q) itself is not regular and does not have d-gon fibres for d > 1.
hypotheses: N >= 1, d | N, r in (Z/(N/d)Z)^x; d > 2 for the identification with a component of the formal completion
Corollary 2.3.3 ensures q^{b/d} is a Gamma_1(N)-structure before descent
proofSteps: Uniqueness of Tate^reg from Thm 2.5.2's final part.

Existence by fppf descent along Spec Z[zeta_N][[q^{1/d}]] -> Spec Z[zeta_{N/d}][[q^{1/d}]]: after q^{1/d} -> zeta_N^{r'b'^{-1}} q^{1/d} one is in the setting of Thm 2.5.2 over A = Z[zeta_N]; descent data exist after inverting q^{1/d}, and extend over q^{1/d} = 0 by Cor. 3.2.5 because Z[zeta_N] tensor_{Z[zeta_{N/d}]} Z[zeta_N] is reduced; effectivity via stability of the ample d-torsion (checked over Z((q))).

The map lands in M^sch (Conrad Thm 4.2.1, since d-gon points with d > 2 have no automorphisms and the only open containing q^{1/d} = 0 is everything); non-smooth locus (q^{1/d}) after scalar extension.

(4.3.8) Spf -> formal completion: the ideal of topological nilpotents pulls back to (q^{1/d}) (Lemma 4.3.2, Thm 4.3.4); on reduced closed subschemes it is an open and closed immersion; both sides regular equidimensional of the same dimension, so it is an open and closed immersion of formal schemes.
acceptance: Cusp width: the local parameter at a d-gon cusp of X_1(N) is q^{1/d}; compare with the analytic width of the cusp (R12.3).
Remark 4.3.5: only the existence of finite flat covers W'[[q^{1/d}]] of deformation rings at cusps with universal structure (Tate_d(zeta q^{1/d}), q^{b/d}) is used later (R14.1).

nodes.title: Cusp charts for d <= 2: degree-2 coverings of infinitesimal neighbourhoods and quadratically twisted Tate curves over Z[zeta_{N/d}]^+[1/delta][[q^{1/d}]]
nodes.statement: For d <= 2, Tate^reg(zeta_{N/d}^{-1} q) with its Gamma_1(N)-structure 'q^{1/d}' induces compatible degree-2 finite flat coverings Spec(Z[zeta_{N/d}][q^{1/d}]/(q^{1/d})^{m+1}) -> M^infinity_{Gamma_1(N),d,m} of the m-th infinitesimal neighbourhoods for all m >= 0, finite etale of degree 2 after inverting delta_{N,d} if N/d > 2. For d <= 2 and N/d > 2, a quadratic twist Tate'_d over Z[zeta_{N/d}]^+[1/delta_{N,d}][[q^{1/d}]] with a descended Gamma_1(N)-structure maps into M^sch_Gamma1(N) and algebraizes the formal completion along M^infinity_{Gamma_1(N),d} over Z[1/delta_{N,d}], compatibly with the coverings (Conrad Thm 4.3.7). Tate'_1 is obtained by etale descent of (Tate_1, zeta_N) along Spec Z[zeta_N][[q]][1/delta] -> Spec Z[zeta_N]^+[[q]][1/delta] using negation; for d = 2 one descends 'q^{1/2}' on Tate^reg(zeta_{N/2}^{-1} q) along the automorphism zeta_{N/2} -> zeta_{N/2}^{-1}, q^{1/2} -> zeta_{N/2}^{-1} q^{1/2}, whose invariant ring is Z[zeta_{N/2}]^+[1/delta][[(1 + zeta_{N/2}^{-1}) q^{1/2}]]; Conrad identifies it with a power series ring Z[zeta_{N/2}]^+[1/delta][[t]], t = (1 + zeta_{N/2}^{-1}) q^{1/2}, using that 1 + zeta_{N/2}^{-1} is a unit in Z[zeta_{N/2}, 1/delta] ('recall N/d > 2, so N >= 5'). Reviewer caveat (not in the source): this unit claim fails when N/2 = 2p^s with p odd, where Def. 4.3.3 gives delta_{N,2} = 1 (for N = 12, 1 + zeta_6^{-1} = 1 - zeta_3 has norm 3 and 2 + zeta_6 + zeta_6^{-1} = 3); these are the cases (4p^s,2) that appear to be misclassified as schematic (see gap), and with delta = p the claim holds.
hypotheses: d <= 2; N/d > 2 for the etaleness and the twisted algebraization; delta_{N,d} = p in partially-schematic cases, 1 in schematic cases
Conrad omits details: 'the proof is essentially the same as that of Theorem 4.3.6'
proofSteps: Nowhere-schematic cases (N/d <= 2) from (4.3.1) and the fibral flatness criterion.
Quadratic descent with negation (DR II 2.8) for d = 1; invariant-ring computation (4.3.10)-(4.3.12) for d = 2.
Cases delta_{N,d} = 1 and delta_{N,d} = p treated separately (details omitted in the source).
acceptance: For N = 5, d = 1 ((5,1) = (p^s,1) is partially schematic with delta_{5,1} = 5): over Z[1/5] the 1-gon cusps of X_1(5) have chart Z[zeta_5]^+[1/5][[q]]; over Q this is a single cusp with residue field Q(zeta_5)^+ = Q(sqrt 5). No schematic chart over Z_(5) is claimed.
The cases N/d <= 2 have no schematic chart at all (stacky cusps).

Negative test (reviewer): for (N,d) = (12,2) the degree-2 map Spec Z[zeta_6][[q^{1/2}]] -> Spec Z[[t]] cannot be finite etale at 3; any formal statement of Thm 4.3.7 must exclude or reclassify (4p^s,2), p odd.

nodes.title: Degeneracy ideals under isogenies: I' = I^d when the kernel meets fibral identity components in rank d
nodes.statement: If f : E -> E' is an isogeny of generalized elliptic curves over S and there is d >= 1 such that for every degenerate geometric fibre E_s the intersection (Ker f)_s with (E_s^sm)^0 has rank d, then the ideal sheaves of the degeneracy loci satisfy I_{S^infinity,E'} = (I_{S^infinity,E})^d (Cesnavicius Prop. 2.2.11); such d exists Zariski-locally on S (Remark 2.2.12). Also f maps E^sing into E'^sing and S^infinity(E) c S^infinity(E') (Prop. 2.2.10).
hypotheses: f an isogeny (surjective homomorphism) of generalized elliptic curves; constant rank d of the kernel on fibral identity components
proofSteps: Reduce to S = Spec R with R artinian local with separably closed residue field and degenerate special fibre; take quotients in stages (Cor. 2.2.7(c)) so that Ker f c (E^sm)^0 or Ker f intersect (E^sm)^0 = 0.
If Ker f meets the identity component trivially, f is finite etale and E^sing = f^{-1}(E'^sing) (SGA 7 VI 5.1(a)), so the loci agree (Lemma 2.1.10).

If Ker f c (E^sm)^0: after a flat cover of S choose a finite etale G c E^sm mapping isomorphically onto the component group of the special fibre, and pass to E/G and E'/f(G) (degeneracy loci unchanged by the previous case) to make E irreducible; by DR VII 2.1 E is a base change of Tate_1 over Z[[q]], and Ker f = mu_d inside (E^sm)^0 (Lemma 2.1.11); Tate_1 -> Tate_1/mu_d is Tate_1 -> Tate_1(q^d) (Example 2.2.1, compare Conrad 2.5.1), and by DR VII 1.11 the degeneracy loci are (q) and (q^d).
acceptance: For Tate_1 over Z[[q]] and f with kernel mu_p: the target degenerates along (q^p), consistent with the p-isogeny q -> q^p in the Hecke correspondence (R14.1).
Cor. 3.2.5 (contractions multiply the ideal by m) is the analogous statement for contractions (R13.2).

nodes.title: The Hodge line omega = e^* Omega^1 on M_Gamma: invertible, base change, insensitive to contraction; finite free H^0(M_Gamma, omega^k); canonical basis dt/t on Tate curves
nodes.statement: For a generalized elliptic curve f : E -> S with identity e in E^sm(S), the pushforward omega_{E/S} of the relative dualizing sheaf is invertible, commutes with base change, and omega_{E/S} = e^* Omega^1_{E/S} canonically (DR II 1.6; Conrad Section 4.4). If D c E^sm is a finite locally free subgroup and E -> Ebar is the contraction away from D, it is an isomorphism near the identity sections, so omega_{E/S} = omega_{Ebar/S}. For Gamma in {Gamma(N), Gamma_1(N), Gamma_0(N)} let omega_Gamma on M_Gamma be omega of the universal generalized elliptic curve; since M_Gamma is proper and flat over Z, H^0(M_Gamma, omega_Gamma^k) is a finite free Z-module (Conrad Section 4.4, using coherence [O]). On Tate curves omega has the canonical generator dt/t coming from (Tate_n)^_0 = G_m-hat (DR VII 1.12 'dx/x'), which is the basis used for q-expansions (Conrad Example 4.5.3). Conrad's Remark 4.4.2 asserts, without proof ('We leave the proof as an exercise'), that f in M_k(Gamma_1(N), C) lies in the image M_{k,Z} iff its q-expansions at all cusps have algebraic integer coefficients and those at the N-gon cusps have coefficients in Z.
hypotheses: Gamma in {Gamma(N), Gamma_1(N), Gamma_0(N)} (Conrad Section 4.4 uses the naive Gamma_0(N) stack)
Coherence of higher direct images for proper Artin stacks [O]
proofSteps: Invertibility and base change of omega from DR II 1.6 (R13.1 stable genus-one node); e lies in the smooth locus where Omega^1 is the dualizing sheaf.
Contraction invariance: the contraction map is an isomorphism on u^{-1}(Ebar^sm) near e.
Finiteness and freeness: coherence for the proper Z-stack plus Z-flatness (torsion-free finitely generated Z-module).
acceptance: The q-expansion of a section at a cusp chart of R13.3 is its value on (Tate^reg, q^{b/d}) written in the basis (dt/t)^k.
Remark 4.4.2 (integrality via q-expansions at all cusps) is not proved in the source; it must not be treated as established (see gap).

nodes.title: The coarse moduli space of Ell_n (and of Ell) is P^1_Z (resp. A^1_Z via j), with formation compatible with arbitrary base change
nodes.statement: (Cesnavicius Lemma 3.3.1) If X is a Deligne-Mumford stack, separated, flat and locally of finite type over Z, with coarse space X, and the coarse space map of X_{F_p} is X_{F_p} for every prime p, then X_S is the coarse space of X_S for every scheme S. (Prop. 3.3.2) For every n >= 1 the coarse moduli space of Ell_n is P^1_Z and that of Ell is A^1_Z (via the j-invariant), and their formation commutes with base change to an arbitrary scheme S; in particular Ell_n is irreducible with geometrically irreducible Z-fibres. For n = 1 over S = Spec Z this is DR VI 1.1, 1.3; locally noetherian S is [FO10, 2.1].

nodes.title: Coarse modular curves |X_H|: projective, normal, finite locally free over the j-line; |X_H| = |X(n)|/H-bar; identification with the Katz-Mazur coarse and compactified coarse moduli schemes
nodes.statement: Notation: X_H is the Deligne-Rapoport stack and |X_H| its coarse moduli space (Cesnavicius uses script and roman letters). For an open H c GL_2(Z-hat), the separated finite type Deligne-Mumford stack X_H has a coarse moduli space |X_H| ([KM97, 1.3(1)]); |Y_H| c |X_H| is the coarse space of the elliptic locus. Since |X(1)| = P^1_Z and |X_H| is Z-proper [Ryd13, 6.12], |X_H| -> P^1_Z is finite, so |X_H| is a projective Z-scheme; |X_H| is normal (inherited from X_H, [AV02, 2.2.3]), so |X_H| -> P^1_Z is locally free of constant rank (EGA IV_2 6.1.5), and |X_H| is flat of relative dimension 1 over Z at every point (Cesnavicius 6.1). If Gamma(n) c H with image H-bar in GL_2(Z/nZ), then |X_H| is the categorical quotient |X(n)|/H-bar (Lemma 6.2 = DR IV 3.10(iii)). Katz-Mazur's quotient moduli problem [Gamma(n)]/H-bar, its coarse moduli scheme M([Gamma(n)]/H-bar) and its compactified coarse moduli scheme M-bar([Gamma(n)]/H-bar) (defined as the normalization of P^1_Z in M) are identified with the stack Y_H, the coarse |Y_H| and the coarse |X_H| respectively (Prop. 6.3); in particular |X_H| is the normalization of the j-line in |Y_H|. |X_H| = X_H (the stack is a scheme) whenever H is small enough (Lemma 4.1.3).
hypotheses: H open in GL_2(Z-hat); n >= 1 with Gamma(n) c H
KM97 existence of coarse spaces for separated stacks with finite inertia
proofSteps: Finiteness of X_H -> P^1_Z from properness and quasi-finiteness; projectivity then follows.
Normality of coarse spaces of normal Deligne-Mumford stacks via etale-local quotient presentations [AV02, 2.2.3].

Prop. 6.3(a): for H = Gamma(n), [Gamma(n)] = Y(n) by the definitions of [KM 5.1, 3.1] and 4.3.1, and Y(n) = Y_Gamma(n) by Thm 4.3.5; general H over Z[1/n] by [KM 7.1.3(2)], over Z by [KM 7.1.3(5)-(6)].
Prop. 6.3(b): if Y_H is representable use (a) and [KM 8.1.1]; in general Lemma 6.2. (c): M-bar is the normalization of P^1_Z in M, and X_H is the normalization of X(1) in Y_H.
acceptance: For prime N >= 5 and a diamond subgroup, the compactified coarse curve over Z[1/N] is the normalization of the j-line in its affine part; any other normal proper model finite over P^1 with the same affine part (e.g. the #81 Layer 10 compactification) must coincide with it by uniqueness of normalization (the #81 object itself was not inspected; see gap).
X_Gamma0(n) coarse space agrees with that of X_0(n)^naive (next nodes).

nodes.title: Coarse |X_H| is Z[1/n]-smooth; its formation commutes with base change over Z[1/gcd(6,n)], and can fail otherwise (X_Gamma1(4) over F_2)
nodes.statement: Let H c GL_2(Z-hat) be open and n >= 1 with Gamma(n) c H; write |.| for coarse moduli spaces. (a) |(X_H)_Z[1/n]| = |X_H|_Z[1/n] is Z[1/n]-smooth (Cesnavicius Prop. 6.4(a); DR VI 6.7 by another method). (b) For any Z[1/gcd(6,n)]-scheme S the canonical map |(X_H)_S| -> |X_H|_S is an isomorphism (Prop. 6.4(b)). The hypothesis that gcd(6,n) be invertible cannot be removed in general: |(X_Gamma1(4))_{F_2}| -> |X_Gamma1(4)|_{F_2} is not an isomorphism (Remark 6.6, citing Cesnavicius 'Coarse base change fails for some modular curves', Thm 3.2). A version of (a) in residue characteristics dividing n for suitable H is [KM 10.10.3(5)] (Remark 6.5).
hypotheses: (a): base Z[1/n]
(b): S a Z[1/gcd(6,n)]-scheme, i.e. locally a Z[1/6]-scheme or a Z[1/n]-scheme
proofSteps: (a): cover X(n^2) by GL_2(Z/n^2Z)-invariant opens affine over Z and preimages of affine opens of X(1); by Lemma 6.2 and [KM, Theorem on p. 508] reduce to H = Gamma(n^2); for n >= 2 geometric points of X(n^2)_Z[1/n] have no automorphisms ([KM 2.7.2(1)], Lemma 2.1.6), so X(n^2)_Z[1/n] is the stack itself and is smooth by DR IV 2.5.

(b) over Z[1/6]: X_H -> X(1) representable, so geometric automorphism groups have order dividing 24; etale-locally X_H = [Spec A/G] with #G | 24 [Ols06, 2.12], and invariants commute with base change when #G is invertible.

(b) over Z[1/n]: by Lemma 3.3.1 reduce to S = Spec F_p with p not dividing n; the finite map from the coarse space of (X_H)_{F_p} to (X_H)_{F_p} is between F_p-smooth curves (DR IV 6.7 and (a)), hence locally free; its rank is 1 because on the preimage U of the complement of j = 0, 1728 the coarse space is compatible with base change (split U into the open and closed V where alpha = [-1]^*(alpha) and its complement, rigidify V by {+-1}).
acceptance: Negative test (required by the README): a statement 'coarse modular curves commute with arbitrary base change' must be rejected; X_Gamma1(4) over F_2 is the counterexample cited.
For H = Gamma_0(p) with p >= 5 prime one may take n = p, so gcd(6, n) = 1 and Prop. 6.4(b) gives coarse base change to every scheme S (not only over Z[1/6]).

nodes.title: Coarse X_0(n): regular after removing j = 0, 1728 in characteristics dividing n; the naive and refined Gamma_0(n) stacks have the same coarse space
nodes.statement: (Cesnavicius Thm 6.7) For n >= 1 the open subscheme U of the coarse space |X_0(n)| obtained by removing the closed points with j = 0 or j = 1728 in residue characteristics dividing n is regular. (Remark 6.8) For squarefree n one may remove only the supersingular such points (via Prop. 6.4 and [KM 13.5.6, Thm on p. 508]), and likewise on reduced components of X_0(n)_{F_p}; [Edi90] studies the coarse space more thoroughly. (Prop. 6.9) The contraction X_0(n)^naive -> X_0(n) induces an isomorphism on coarse moduli spaces; (Remark 6.10) likewise the coarse spaces of X_1(n;n') and X_0(n;n') agree with those of X_Gamma1(n;n') and X_Gamma0(n;n') for all n, n'. This regularity was known ([Edi90, 1.2] by explicit completion computations; [GZ86, Prop. III.1.4]); Cesnavicius's proof uses the refined moduli interpretation.
hypotheses: n >= 1 arbitrary
proofSteps: Over Z[1/n] regularity is Prop. 6.4(a).

On the preimage U of P^1 minus {j = 0, 1728}, the automorphism group of the universal object of X_0(n) is exactly {+-1}_U ([Del75, 5.3(III)] and representability of X_0(n) -> X(1)), so the coarse space of U is the rigidification U // {+-1}; U -> U // {+-1} is etale [AOV08, A.1] and U is regular (Thm 5.13(a)).

Prop. 6.9: the coarse space X_0(n)' of X_0(n)^naive exists (finite diagonal, [Ryd13, 6.12]) and is finite over P^1_Z with the same elliptic locus, so it suffices that it is normal; for U c X_0(n)^naive with affine coarse space Spec A, A = Gamma(U, O_U) is integrally closed because U is normal (Thm 4.6.4(a)) and generizations lift along smooth atlases [LMB00, 5.7.1].
acceptance: At n = p^2 the coarse spaces of X_0(p^2)^naive and X_0(p^2) coincide although the stacks differ at the cusps.

Theorem 6.7 makes no claim at the removed points (j = 0 or 1728 in residue characteristics dividing n); Remark 6.8 allows restricting the removed points to supersingular ones for squarefree n. No statement that regularity fails there was read.

nodes.title: Compactified level stacks have geometrically connected fibres over Z (Gamma_1(N;n)) and over Z[zeta_N] (Gamma(N)), using connectedness of the complex fibre
nodes.statement: Let M = M_Gamma considered over S = Spec Z for Gamma = Gamma_1(N;n) and over S = Spec Z[zeta_N] (via the Weil-pairing morphism) for Gamma = Gamma(N). Then the proper flat map M -> S has geometrically connected fibres (Conrad Thm 4.2.1(1)). In particular the fixed-pairing fibres of the full-level compactified stack are geometrically connected in every characteristic, including characteristics dividing N.
hypotheses: Gamma in {Gamma(N), Gamma_1(N;n)} with Conrad's conditions
Coherence and the theorem on formal functions for proper Artin stacks [O] (Zariski connectedness via Stein factorization)
Connectedness of the complex fibre of M^0 (analytic input)
proofSteps: By [O], Stein factorizations of proper maps of locally noetherian Artin stacks have geometrically connected fibres.

M -> S is proper flat with smooth generic fibre and S is connected and normal, so f is its own Stein factorization, hence has geometrically connected fibres, provided the geometric generic fibre is connected.
Since M^infinity is a relative effective Cartier divisor and fibres have pure dimension 1, connectedness of a fibre follows from connectedness of the complement of M^infinity in it.

Connectedness of the complex fibre of M^0 'follows (upon adjoining a little level) from comparison with the complex-analytic theory' (not spelled out in the source; supplied by ModularCurvesPartII:R12.4).
acceptance: Over Z (not Z[zeta_N]) the full-level stack M_Gamma(N) has phi(N) geometric components in characteristic 0: connectedness must be stated over Z[zeta_N].
The statement over Spec Z[zeta_N] includes fibres over primes dividing N, which do not follow from the complex statement alone without the Stein-factorization argument.

nodes.title: C tensor H^0(M_Gamma, omega^k) = M_k(Gamma, C) for Gamma(N), Gamma_1(N), Gamma_0(N); Gamma_0 forms are the (Z/NZ)^x-invariants; compatibility with diamond operators
nodes.statement: By Conrad Remark 4.1.5, M_Gamma(N) over Z[zeta_N] agrees with the stack M_N constructed by normalization in DR IV Section 3; hence by DR VII Section 4, using Z[zeta_N] -> C with zeta_N -> e^{2 pi i/N}, there is a canonical isomorphism C tensor_{Z[zeta_N]} H^0(M_Gamma(N), omega^k) = M_k(Gamma(N), C) (4.4.1) for k >= 0, and by the same methods C tensor H^0(M_Gamma1(N), omega^k) = M_k(Gamma_1(N), C) and C tensor H^0(M_Gamma0(N), omega^k) = M_k(Gamma_0(N), C) (4.4.2). These Z-structures are compatible with (4.4.1) via the finite flat maps M_Gamma(N) -> M_Gamma1(N) -> M_Gamma0(N) (Lemma 4.2.3), which are pullback-compatible with omega; they are generally not the Z-structures defined by q-expansions at a single cusp. The (Z/NZ)^x action on the universal Gamma_1(N)-structure induces an action on omega_Gamma1(N) compatible with the diamond operators on M_k(Gamma_1(N), C), and H^0(M_Gamma0(N), omega^k) is exactly the submodule of (Z/NZ)^x-invariants in H^0(M_Gamma1(N), omega^k) (Lemma 4.4.1).
hypotheses: Gamma_0(N) here is Conrad's (naive) stack; for non-squarefree N it is not X_Gamma0(N) (R13.2), although both have the same coarse space

The analytic comparison is DR VII 4.6 (read by the reviewer on the page images of printed pp. 310-313): it treats full level n only, for the fibre M_n (x)_{Z[zeta_n]} C; Conrad asserts the Gamma_1(N) and Gamma_0(N) cases of (4.4.2) 'by the same methods', without further proof
proofSteps: Remark 4.1.5 identifies M_Gamma(N)/Z[zeta_N] with DR's normalization M_N (DR IV 3). DR VII 4.6: for n >= 3, M_n (x)_{Z[zeta_n]} C is a scheme whose open part has underlying analytic space X/Ker(SL(2,Z) -> SL(2,Z/n)) (X the upper half-plane); holomorphic sections of omega^k there are the holomorphic functions satisfying the weight-k transformation law 4.5(A); such a section extends over the cusps iff it satisfies the boundedness condition 4.5(B); by GAGA these are the algebraic sections. General n is reduced to level 3n by taking invariants under Ker(SL(2,Z/3n) -> SL(2,Z/n)) (the scan prints 'poids 3n', evidently meaning level 3n). DR VII 4.7: q-expansions are obtained by evaluating on the analytic Tate curve (4.3), up to a power of 2 pi i depending on normalizations, and agree with the algebraic expansions of VII 3 by the compatibility 4.4.
Compatibility across Gamma(N), Gamma_1(N), Gamma_0(N) by pullback along the finite flat maps of Lemma 4.2.3 with pi^* omega_Gamma0(N) = omega_Gamma1(N).

Lemma 4.4.1: omega_Gamma0(N)^k c pi_*(omega_Gamma1(N)^k) = omega_Gamma0(N)^k tensor pi_* O, so reduce to O_{M_Gamma0(N)} = (pi_* O_{M_Gamma1(N)})^{(Z/NZ)^x}; both stacks are normal and Z-flat and pi is finite flat, so check over Z[1/N], where pi is a finite etale (Z/NZ)^x-torsor.

The embedding convention zeta_N -> e^{2 pi i/N} must match the analytic Weil pairing convention of R12.1-R12.2.

nodes.title: Formal criterion for extending a morphism from a dense open of a normal Deligne-Mumford stack (Conrad Lemma 4.4.5)
nodes.statement: Let B be a scheme, S a normal locally noetherian Deligne-Mumford stack over B whose strictly henselian local rings are G-rings, M a Deligne-Mumford stack over B that is separated and locally of finite presentation, S' c S a dense open substack and f' : S' -> M a B-morphism. If a morphism f : S -> M with an isomorphism alpha : f|S' = f' exists, the pair (f, alpha) is unique up to unique isomorphism; and such a pair exists iff it exists over the completion of the strictly henselian local ring at each point of S outside S'.
hypotheses: S normal, locally noetherian Deligne-Mumford, strictly henselian local rings G-rings (equivalently on one smooth scheme cover, Remark 4.4.6 and Thm 2.2.8)
M separated, locally of finite presentation, Deligne-Mumford
proofSteps: Uniqueness: etale-locally S is a scheme; Isom of two extensions is represented by a finite S-scheme (M separated Deligne-Mumford), and S-points over the dense open S' extend uniquely over the normal S.

Existence is etale-local by uniqueness; by 'smearing out' at generic points of S - S' and noetherian induction reduce to S = Spec R local with S' the punctured spectrum, and replace R by its strict henselization.

R is a G-ring, so R -> R-hat is regular and Popescu's theorem writes R-hat as a filtered limit of essentially smooth residually trivial local R-algebras; the solution over R-hat descends to a smooth R-algebra A with a rational point in the closed fibre, and henselianity gives an R-section, pulling back to a solution over R.
acceptance: Locate the use of each hypothesis in the proof: normality of S and separatedness of M (finite Isom-schemes) give uniqueness, the G-ring condition gives regularity of R -> R-hat for Popescu's theorem, and henselianity gives the section. The source gives no counterexample for non-normal S or non-separated M, and none is claimed here.

nodes.title: The p-th Hecke correspondence pi_1, pi_2 : M_Gamma1(N;p) => M_Gamma1(N) and the pullback map xi on omega extend uniquely and are finite flat over Z
nodes.statement: For any N >= 1 and prime p, the maps pi'_1(E;P,C) = (E,P) and pi'_2(E;P,C) = (E/C, P mod C) on the elliptic loci M^0_Gamma1(N;p) => M^0_Gamma1(N) extend uniquely to finite flat morphisms pi_1, pi_2 : M_Gamma1(N;p) => M_Gamma1(N) over Z, and the pullback map xi' : (pi'_2)^* omega_Gamma1(N) -> omega_Gamma1(N;p) along the universal p-isogeny extends uniquely to xi : pi_2^* omega_Gamma1(N) -> omega_Gamma1(N;p) (Conrad Thm 1.2.2 = Thm 4.4.3). Here P mod C is a Z/NZ-structure on E/C by Thm 2.3.2(1) and Lemma 2.4.4 (Remark 4.4.4). The essential content is extending pi'_2 over the cusps, where the quotient E/C does not make sense as a generalized elliptic curve (C meeting the identity component of a degenerate fibre).
hypotheses: N >= 1, p prime (M_Gamma1(N;p) = X_Gamma1(N;p) by Cesnavicius Thm 4.6.6(b), since ord_q(p) <= ord_q(N) + 1 for all q)
M_Gamma1(N;p) normal with M^infinity a Cartier divisor; M_Gamma1(N) separated Deligne-Mumford
proofSteps: Uniqueness from finiteness of Isom-schemes (Thm 3.2.2), normality of M_Gamma1(N;p) and the Cartier divisor M^infinity.

pi_1 is the finite flat contraction (E;P,C) -> (c(E), P) of Lemma 4.2.3 (c(E) = contraction away from

).

Let Z c M^infinity_Gamma1(N;p) be the open and closed substack where C meets the fibral identity component (C_0 = mu_p in the standard polygon); off Z, E/C is a generalized elliptic curve (Conrad Ex. 2.1.6) and (E/C, P mod C) and pullback along E -> E/C define pi'_2 and xi' there.

By Lemma 4.4.5 (with B = Spec Z, S = M_Gamma1(N;p), M = M_Gamma1(N)) and the analogous argument for xi, it suffices to extend over complete local rings A at geometric points (E_0;P_0,C_0) in Z, with E_0 a standard d-gon, C_0 = mu_p, <P_0> ample.
By Remark 4.3.5 A has a finite flat cover A' = W'[[q^{1/d}]] over which (E,P) = (Tate_d(zeta q^{1/d}), q^{b/d}); (A' tensor_A A')/a is reduced, so by Cor. 3.2.3 it suffices to work over A'.

Over W'((q^{1/d})), Tate_d(zeta q^{1/d}) = Tate_1(zeta^d q) (Thm 2.5.2) respecting mu_p and G_m-hat; by Example 2.5.1 Tate_1(zeta^d q)/mu_p = Tate_1(zeta^{dp} q^p), which extends to E-bar = Tate_{dp}(zeta q^{1/d}) over W'[[q^{1/d}]]; the quotient map induces the p-th power on G_m-hat, so the map of formal groups (hence xi) extends; P mod C extends to a section of E-bar^sm away from the identity components.

Finite flat: pi_2 quasi-finite hence flat (Lemma 4.1.3), proper, and representable (Cor. 2.2.7, Thm 2.2.5(2)) because points of Z have no automorphisms in their pi_2-fibres (for d > 2 by schematicity of M^infinity_{Gamma_1(N),d}; for d <= 2 because pi_2(y) lives on a blow-up of E_0 containing E_0^sm).
acceptance: Over C, (4.5.1) Tr o xi^k o pi_2^* recovers p T_p (next node), so the correspondence is the classical one.

At a point of Z with (E,P) = (Tate_d(zeta q^{1/d}), q^{b/d}) and C = mu_p, E/C extends to Tate_dp(zeta q^{1/d}), a dp-gon that is an iterated blow-up of E mod q^{1/d} (Conrad p. 45). pi_2 then needs the contraction that makes

ample ('we may apply a contraction', p. 44). The source does not state the resulting polygon. Reviewer computation: P mod C lies on the components of index in pZ/dpZ, so the contraction is a d-gon with parameter zeta^p q^{p/d}. Hence pi_2 is ramified of index p at this cusp and does not multiply the number of sides by p.

nodes.title: Cesnavicius's direct construction: pi_1(E,alpha,H) = (c_alpha(E), alpha), pi_2(E,alpha,H) = (E/H, alpha) on X_Gamma1(n;p) for squarefree p are representable, finite locally free and surjective
nodes.statement: For n >= 1 and squarefree p >= 1 (not necessarily coprime to n), using the moduli interpretations X_Gamma1(n) = X_1(n) and X_Gamma1(n;p) = X_1(n;p), the maps pi_1((E, alpha, H)) = (c_alpha(E), alpha) and pi_2((E, alpha, H)) = (E/H, alpha) (well defined by Prop. 4.2.11(b)) are representable, finite locally free and surjective, hence give a Hecke correspondence X_Gamma1(n;p) => X_Gamma1(n) (Cesnavicius Lemma 4.7.1); pullback of differentials along E -> E/H gives a map (e')^* Omega^1_{(E/H)/S} -> e^* Omega^1_{E/S} of formation compatible with base change, recovering Conrad's xi. For p prime this is the correspondence of Conrad Thm 4.4.3, obtained without extending from the elliptic locus.
hypotheses: n >= 1; p >= 1 squarefree
Quotients E/H by arbitrary finite locally free subgroups (R13.1 quotient node)
proofSteps: pi_1 is the X(1)-morphism induced by Gamma_1(n;p) c Gamma_1(n), finite by 4.1.2; flat by EGA IV_2 6.1.5 since X_Gamma1(n) is regular (Thm 4.4.4(a)); surjectivity checked over (Y_Gamma1(n))_Q.
pi_2 representable by Lemma 3.2.2(b): an automorphism i of E stabilizing H and inducing the identity on E/H fixes (E^sm)^0 because id - i on E^sm factors through H.
pi_2 proper (properness of both stacks), quasi-finite on geometric fibres, hence finite (Lemma 3.2.3); flat by EGA IV_2 6.1.5; surjective over (Y_Gamma1(n))_Q.
acceptance: For p = l_1 l_2 squarefree the correspondence is the composite-degree isogeny correspondence; for p | n it is the U_p-type correspondence.
Non-squarefree p is not covered by Lemma 4.7.1.

nodes.title: Conrad's Gamma_0 variant: pi~_1, pi~_2 : M_Gamma0(N;p) => M_Gamma0(N) finite flat, and xi~ by descent (on the naive Gamma_0 stacks)
nodes.statement: For positive N, n with ord_q(n) <= ord_q(N) for q | gcd(N,n), a Gamma_0(N;n)-structure is (G, C) with G c E^sm cyclic of order N and C cyclic of order n such that, fppf-locally where G has a generator P, (P, C) is a Gamma_1(N;n)-structure. M_Gamma1(N;n) -> M_Gamma0(N;n) is finite flat of degree phi(N), and M_Gamma0(N;n) is a proper flat regular Artin stack over Z with geometrically connected fibres of pure dimension 1 whose boundary is a Z-flat Cartier divisor. pi~_1(E;G,C) = (c(E), G) is representable and finite flat; pi~_2 (E/C, G mod C), defined off the boundary, extends to a finite flat morphism by factoring pi_2 through the finite flat cover M_Gamma1(N;p) -> M_Gamma0(N;p) using Cor. 3.2.3 and reducedness of M^infinity_Gamma1(N;p) x_{M^infinity_Gamma0(N;p)} M^infinity_Gamma1(N;p); xi~ is obtained by descent of xi (Conrad end of Section 4.4). Caveat (R13.2): these are the naive Gamma_0 stacks (Cesnavicius 4.6.2 identifies Conrad's M_Gamma0(N;n) with his X_0(n;n'), n = N, n' = n). By Cesnavicius Thm 4.6.6(c), X_0(N;p) = X_Gamma0(N;p) holds if |ord_q(p) - ord_q(N)| <= 1 for all primes q, i.e. if ord_q(N) <= 1 for q != p and ord_p(N) <= 2. This is a sufficient condition; the sources read do not state that it is necessary for n' = p. The naive X_0(N) = X_0(N;1) differs from X_Gamma0(N) when p^2 | N (Cesnavicius 1.2, 5.1).
hypotheses: ord_q(n) <= ord_q(N) for q | gcd(N,n) (Conrad)
Correct stack identification requires the squarefreeness conditions stated in the caveat
proofSteps: The Cartier divisor sum over j in Z/mZ of (j(N/m)P + C) is independent of the generator P (Z-flatness of Gamma_1(N;n) deformation rings, finite flatness of generator schemes, Thm 2.3.7).
Properties of M_Gamma0(N;n) inferred from M_Gamma1(N;n) (details indicated only briefly: 'one infers').

pi~_2: Lemma 4.4.5 does not apply (M_Gamma0(N;p) often not Deligne-Mumford); instead descend pi_2 along the finite flat M_Gamma1(N;p) -> M_Gamma0(N;p) using Cor. 3.2.3, the needed reducedness following from flatness and Lemma 4.3.2.
acceptance: For squarefree N prime to p, the correspondence is on X_Gamma0(N;p) = X_0(N;p) and gives the classical T_p on Gamma_0(N).

For N = q^2 (q != p), Thm 4.6.6(c) does not apply to M_Gamma0(q^2;p) (|0 - 2| = 2 > 1). Whether it differs from X_Gamma0(q^2;p) is not stated in the sources read; the mu_q-automorphism example of Cesnavicius 1.2 suggests it does. A Hecke correspondence on the refined X_0(q^2) is not constructed in the sources read.

nodes.title: Hecke operators T_p on M_{k,Z} = H^0(M_Gamma1(N), omega^k) over Z, including p | N: Tr o xi^k o pi_2^* has image in p M_{k,Z}
nodes.statement: Since omega is insensitive to contraction, pi_1^* omega_Gamma1(N) = omega_Gamma1(N;p), and pi_1 finite flat gives a trace Tr : H^0(M_Gamma1(N;p), omega^k) -> H^0(M_Gamma1(N), omega^k) = M_{k,Z}. The composite (4.5.1) Tr o xi^k o pi_2^* : M_{k,Z} -> M_{k,Z} recovers p T_p on the complex fibre. (Conrad Thm 4.5.1) For K separably closed, x : Spec K -> M_Gamma1(N), y in pi_1^{-1}(x), with strictly henselian local rings R_x, R_y (R_y finite flat over R_x) and R_{pi_2(y)}, the composite of stalk maps omega_{pi_2(y)} -> omega_{Gamma_1(N;p),y} = R_y tensor_{R_x} omega_x -> omega_x (xi_y then Tr_{y|x}) has image in p.omega_x. Hence (4.5.1) has image in p M_{k,Z}, T_p = p^{-1}(4.5.1) preserves the Z-structure M_{k,Z} for all p (even p | N), and eigenvalues of classical Hecke operators are algebraic integers, without q-expansions or topological cohomology.
hypotheses: Gamma_1(N), any N >= 1, any prime p, weight k
The comparison of (4.5.1) with classical p T_p over C uses the analytic comparison (4.4.2) and the classical formula T_p = (1/p) Tr_{pi'_1} o (xi')^k o (pi'_2)^* on meromorphic forms
proofSteps: Global from local: the image of (4.5.1) lies in p M_{k,Z} if it does stalkwise at strictly henselian local rings.

Theorem 4.5.1: assume char K = p; by normality of the moduli stacks ignore the codimension-2 locus of cusps in characteristic p (Conrad p. 46). The supersingular points in characteristic p, where C_0 is neither multiplicative nor etale, are not mentioned in the source. They also form a codimension-2 locus of the normal stacks, so the same normality argument (a section of p^{-1} omega regular in codimension one is regular) disposes of them (reviewer's observation). Work modulo p.
If C_0 is multiplicative, the universal p-isogeny over R_y/(p) has kernel mu_p, so xi_y kills invariant differentials in characteristic p.

If C_0 is etale (E_0 ordinary), R-hat_y/(p) over R-hat_x/(p) classifies splittings of the connected-etale sequence, which by fppf Kummer theory is extraction of a p-th root of a unit; extensions A -> A[X]/(X^p - u) in characteristic p have vanishing trace (universal case F_p[u] -> F_p[u,X]/(X^p - u) is purely inseparable).
acceptance: Over C with p not dividing N, p^{-1}(4.5.1) is the usual T_p on M_k(Gamma_1(N), C); with p | N it is U_p.
The trace through the inseparable (etale-C in characteristic p) situation is shown to vanish mod p rather than divided by the degree naively, matching the README's warning about inseparable traces.

nodes.title: T_l on weight-k Katz forms for Gamma_1(N) over F_p (any k, including k = 1 and l = p) via local lifts, and its q-expansion formulas at (Tate_1, zeta)
nodes.statement: (Conrad Lemma 4.5.2) If M is a locally noetherian Deligne-Mumford stack and F a Cohen-Macaulay coherent sheaf, compatible stalk elements s_x over strictly henselian local rings glue to a unique global section. Using the finite flat Hecke correspondence and xi over Z, for any prime l and Katz form f of weight k and level N over F_p, (f|T_l)_x = sum over y in pi_1^{-1}(x) of (l^{-1} Tr_{y|x}(xi(pi_2^*(F_{pi_2(y)})))) mod p, where F_{pi_2(y)} lifts f_{pi_2(y)} to the stalk over R_{pi_2(y)} (or modulo p^2); by Thm 4.5.1 for l = p the trace lies in l.omega_x, the result is independent of the lift, compatible with localization, and M_Gamma1(N)/F_p is CM, so the stalks glue to f|T_l in H^0(M_Gamma1(N)/F_p, omega^k). (Example 4.5.3) For p not dividing N, k >= 1, zeta a primitive N-th root of unity in F_p-bar, with f(Tate_1, zeta) = (sum a_n q^n)(dt/t)^k and (f|<l>)(Tate_1, zeta) = (sum b_n q^n)(dt/t)^k: (f|T_l)(Tate_1, zeta) = (sum_{n>=1} a_{nl} q^n + l^{k-1} sum_{n>=1} b_n q^{nl})(dt/t)^k if l does not divide N, and (sum_{n>=1} a_{nl} q^n)(dt/t)^k if l | N, deduced from characteristic 0 by the method of construction (formulas checked on the page image of p. 48).
hypotheses: Lemma 4.5.2: M locally noetherian Deligne-Mumford, F Cohen-Macaulay coherent
Example 4.5.3: p not dividing N, k >= 1, l any prime (possibly l = p)
proofSteps: Lemma 4.5.2: reduce to M = Spec A affine with M of full support; CM implies every associated prime of M is minimal, so equalities can be tested at minimal primes and elements glue by smearing out and etale descent.

Construction: lift stalks, apply xi and the finite flat trace, divide by l (possible by Thm 4.5.1 when l = p), reduce mod p; independence of lifts mod l.p; compatibility with specialization since pi_2 is finite and strict henselization commutes with finite algebras.

Example 4.5.3: f is a Katz form over F_p-bar with zeta in mu_N(F_p-bar); work over F_p-bar((q)). Tate_1 over F_p-bar((q)) is the reduction of Tate_1 over W(F_p-bar)((q)), where the formulas are the classical ones, and the construction commutes with reduction of etale-local lifts (finite flat pi_1, finite pi_2, and strict henselization compatible with finite algebras).
acceptance: Weight one: T_p on weight-1 Katz forms mod p (p not dividing N) is defined without global lifting, compare Gross [G, Section 4] where T_p was defined by the q-expansion formula.

Constant terms: as printed, both sums start at n >= 1, so the displayed formula omits the constant term a_0 + l^{k-1} b_0 (resp. a_0) of a non-cuspidal form; for forms non-vanishing at the cusp (Tate_1, zeta) the sums should start at n >= 0 (worker's observation; see gap).

gaps.title: Conrad's nodal-cubic model of the standard 1-gon is incorrect over Z
gaps.detail: Verified on the page image of Conrad's preprint p. 5: 'The map t -> (t^2+1, t(t^2+1)) from P^1 to the nodal plane curve y^2z = x^3 - x^2z factorizes through C_1 and induces an isomorphism'. Worker's computation (not in any source): this map sends t = i and t = -i to the node and t = 0, infinity to the distinct points (1:0:1), (0:1:0), so it does not glue 0 and infinity; the node of y^2 = x^2(x-1) has tangent slopes +-i (non-split over Q) and the curve is cuspidal in characteristic 2. Nothing else in Conrad uses this model. Next action: a reviewer should confirm and, if a Weierstrass model of C_1 over Z is wanted, verify a split nodal cubic such as y^2 z + xyz = x^3 (or take C_1 as defined by gluing). Review (REVIEW-EXT-12): Page image of Conrad p. 5 checked: 'The map t |-> (t^2 + 1, t(t^2 + 1)) from P^1 to the nodal plane curve y^2z = x^3 - x^2z factorizes through C_1 and induces an isomorphism between C_1 and this nodal cubic.' Reviewer's algebra (sympy): the map does land on the curve; x = 0 exactly at t = +-i, so it glues i and -i, not 0 and infinity (t = 0 -> (1:0:1), t = infinity -> (0:1:0)); the tangent cone at the node is x^2 + y^2 (slopes +-i, a non-split node over Q, so the curve is not isomorphic to C_1 even over Q); in characteristic 2 the tangent cone is (x + y)^2 and the singularity is a cusp. The only occurrence of the model in Conrad is this sentence. The drafter's replacement is correct: for W : y^2z + xyz = x^3 the map (s:u) |-> (su(u - s) : s^2u : (u - s)^3) sends 0 and infinity to the node (0:0:1) and 1 to (0:1:0); the tangent cone y(y + x) is split in every characteristic; c_4 = 1 and Delta = 0; the only singular point is the node. Hence the induced C_1 -> W is an isomorphism on geometric fibres of flat proper Z-schemes and so an isomorphism (EGA IV_4 17.9.5). Conrad's cubic does become isomorphic to C_1 over Z[i, 1/2] (the Mobius map sending 0, infinity to i, -i has determinant 2i). All of this is reviewer computation, not source text.

gaps.detail: Conrad (p. 16) states Lemma 2.4.7 'whose proof goes as in the higher-genus case in [DM, 1.2]'. DM Thm 1.2 (Publ. Math. IHES 36 (1969), public Numdam copy, read by the reviewer) is about stable curves of genus g >= 2: H^1(C, omega^{n}) = 0 for n >= 2 and omega^{n} very ample for n >= 3, proved by positivity of degrees on components, duality and the very-ampleness criterion H^1(C, m_x m_y L) = 0 checked at smooth and double points (three cases). Not written in any source: the genus-one adaptation with O(rD) (using omega_{C_s} = O and deg O(D)|_E >= 1 on every component, which gives vanishing for r >= 1 and very ampleness for r >= 3) and the relative statement (local freeness of f_*O(rD) of rank rd with base change, surjectivity of f^*f_*O(rD) -> O(rD), closed immersion into P(f_*O(rD))). Next action: write this adaptation, in particular DM's double-point case analysis for r >= 3 on Neron polygons, and add DM 1969 as a packet source.

gaps.title: Conrad Def. 4.3.3 appears to omit the cases (N, d) = (4p^s, 2), p odd: non-schematic 2-gon cusps of M_Gamma1(N) in characteristic p
gaps.detail: Reviewer finding, not in any source read. Conrad p. 38 states that M^infinity_{Gamma_1(N),2} is not a scheme in characteristic p > 0 iff N = 2p^s, and Def. 4.3.3 classifies (N,d) accordingly. Computation: on the standard 2-gon over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p, an ample Gamma_1(N)-structure is P = (x,1) with x^2 a primitive (N/2)'-th root of unity ((N/2)' the prime-to-p part), since 2P must generate mu_{N/2} in the Drinfeld sense. Inversion (x,1) -> (x^{-1},1) fixes P iff x^2 = 1 (N = 2p^s, Conrad's case); inversion followed by -1 in mu_2 on component 1 fixes P iff x^2 = -1, possible for p odd exactly when N = 4p^s. For s >= 1 (e.g. N = 12, p = 3; N = 20, p = 5) such points are non-schematic, so (4p^s,2) should be partially schematic with delta = p. Supporting evidence: Conrad's proof of Lemma 3.1.8 (p. 22) singles out 'd = 2 and P = (x,1) with x^2 in mu_2(k)'; for N = 12, Thm 4.3.4 (M^infinity = Spec Z[zeta_6]^+ = Spec Z) and Thm 4.3.7 (Spec Z[zeta_6] -> M^infinity finite etale, delta = 1) are incompatible because Z[zeta_3] ramifies at 3; and the unit claim 1 + zeta_{N/2}^{-1} in Z[zeta_{N/2}, 1/delta]^x behind (4.3.11) fails exactly in these cases. Thm 4.2.1(2) (d >= 5 inverted) is unaffected. Next action: orchestrator to log as a source issue (errata) against Conrad 2007, Def. 4.3.3 / p. 38 / (4.3.11), and have a second reader confirm; N32's sentence on when M^infinity_{Gamma_1(N),2} is a scheme needs the same caveat. Second reading (lead reviewer): confirmed. With N = 4p^s and p odd in characteristic p, the divisor sum_j [j(i,1)] = p^s([(1,0)] + [(i,1)] + [(-1,0)] + [(-i,1)]) is the subgroup scheme mu_{2p^s} x {0} union i.mu_{2p^s} x {1} of order 4p^s. It meets both components, so P = (i,1) is an ample Drinfeld Z/NZ-structure. tau(x,j) = (x^{-1},-j) followed by -1 in mu_2 fixes it. Conrad's own proof of Thm 4.3.7 (p. 42) sets delta_{N,d} = p when N/d = 2p^s, which for d = 2 gives N = 4p^s and contradicts Def. 4.3.3 (p. 38, page image).

review.notes: Independent review of ModularCurvesPartII.json (53 nodes, 99 links, 21 gaps, 20 coverage records). All three cited sources were obtained publicly with SHA-256 identical to the drafter's library copies: Conrad's preprint (Stanford), Cesnavicius arXiv:1511.07475v2, and the Deligne-Rapoport scan hosted by Rapoport (Bonn). No node is therefore unverifiable. Every node's statement, hypotheses, proof steps, acceptance items, locators and excerpts were compared with the cited passages (whole Conrad and Cesnavicius papers; DR II, III 1.1-1.2 and 2.1-2.6, IV 1.1-1.6 and 2.1-2.2, V 1.1-1.4 and 4.9-4.13, VII 1-2 and 4). Formulas were checked on page images. Also read by the reviewers: Deligne-Mumford 1969 Thm 1.2 (Numdam), and Cesnavicius arXiv:1608.01249v2 Thm 3.2. Result: 19 nodes verified, 34 corrected (75 field corrections), 0 unverifiable. Links: 84 kept, 14 annotated, 1 removed (a node-level cycle), 66 added where a proof read uses a supplier. Gaps: 3 resolved, 10 corrected, 8 confirmed, 6 added (21 -> 24). Main findings: Conrad Thm 3.2.7's 'Deligne-Mumford iff n squarefree' is false in the 'only if' direction (counterexample N = n = p^2); Conrad Def. 4.3.3 omits the non-schematic cusps (4p^s,2), p odd (e.g. N = 12 in characteristic 3); Conrad's '[DR, III, 2.5(iii)]' has no referent; the nodal-cubic model of the 1-gon is wrong (confirmed); the n = 12 d(m) example, the Cesnavicius Prop. 4.3.6 n = 1 case, the pi_2 cusp-width claim and several acceptance items were wrong. Structural issue: three results used by R13.2 proofs are placed in R13.1, R13.3 and R13.4a. They are recorded as gaps with a placement question, since linking them would create stage cycles. No cycle in the union of atlas stageEdges and the packet's links, with or without the reviewer's changes. implementationStatus stays 'unchecked'.
